source_record.support_text: The active metabolite of dilept, N-caproyl-L-prolyl-L-tyrosine, crossed the blood-brain barrier and was detected in the rat brain with a brain/plasma distribution coefficient of 0.5.

In rats, norketamine (2) was taken up rapidly from the systemic circulation into the brain, and the ratio of its concentration in brain tissue to plasma was greater than unity at all time points, indicating it crosses the blood-brain barrier readily.

DG-041 was measured in the brain of male C57BL/6 mice at 1-, 4-, and 8-hour time points following subcutaneous injection, and the compound was found in all three brains, indicating that DG-041 crosses the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Presence of DG-041 was confirmed in the brain at 1, 4, and 8 hours post-SC injection.

source_record.support_text: After oral administration of bergapten for 15 min, it was detected in the cerebrospinal fluid and brain of rats, indicating that it could cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Detection occurred 15 minutes after oral administration.

source_record.support_text: [123I]-R(−)DOI displayed good brain uptake and localized in serotonergic areas of baboon brain.
source_record.extra_details: Examined as a [123I] radiolabeled SPECT imaging agent; it showed high nonspecific uptake.

source_record.support_text: Sargent and colleagues demonstrated the preferential accumulation of radioactivity in brain after administration of radio-labelled DOI (1-(2,5-dimethoxy-4-iodophenyl)-2-aminopropane).

Using whole-body scintigraphy, Sargent et al. showed brain accumulation of radioactivity after administration of a radiolabelled version of 1-(2,5-dimethoxy-4-iodophenyl)-2-aminopropane (DOI) in humans.

Studies conducted by the World Health Organization found that C14-labeled tBHQ could be detected in the brain after dietary administration to rodents, suggesting that tBHQ is able to pass the blood-brain barrier through this route.
source_record.extra_details: detection of C14-labeled tBHQ in the brain

source_record.support_text: Autoradiographic studies have shown that systemically injected radioactive sulpiride labels the pituitary, but not the brain, suggesting that sulpiride penetrates the blood-brain barrier poorly.
Sulpiride had a Kp.uu value well below unity, which may indicate impaired diffusion over the BBB or active efflux, and has been shown to have low permeability.
source_record.extra_details: May indicate impaired diffusion or active efflux.

source_record.support_text: Animal studies have indicated that sulpiride passes fairly slowly through the blood-brain barrier, which may be related to a high plasma vs brain concentration ratio for the molecule.
source_record.extra_details: The text suggests this slow penetration may be related to a high plasma vs brain concentration ratio.

source_record.support_text: Sulpiride showed brain/serum ratios below 1, indicating that entry into the brain is slow.
source_record.extra_details: The drug is reported to be extremely hydrophilic.

source_record.support_text: Sulpiride penetrates relatively poorly into the central nervous system. Injection of tracer amounts of [³H]sulpiride resulted in little or no radioactivity in areas of the brain known to accumulate other benzamide neuroleptics.
source_record.extra_details: Tracer amounts of [³H]sulpiride showed little or no radioactivity in brain areas where other benzamide neuroleptics typically accumulate.

source_record.support_text: There were measurable drug levels in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in all sulpiride-treated patients.
source_record.extra_details: Measurable drug levels were found in the cerebrospinal fluid.

source_record.support_text: Sulpiride is highly hydrophilic and possesses poor liposolubility, which may interfere with its penetration through the blood-brain barrier. This was demonstrated by the fact that 14C-sulpiride administered intraperitoneally to rats could not be detected in the brain tissue.
source_record.extra_details: The poor penetration is attributed to the molecule being highly hydrophilic and having poor liposolubility.

source_record.support_text: In an ex vivo biodistribution study in normal mice, the radiotracer [¹⁸F]8c could not enter the brain through the blood–brain barrier, showing a brain uptake of 0.34 ± 0.05 %ID/g at 60 min.
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 60 min post-injection.

source_record.support_text: Preliminary PET imaging studies of [¹¹C]13 carried out in Sprague–Dawley rats showed excellent brain permeability with a maximum SUV value of 3.6 at 3 min in striatum.
source_record.extra_details: Maximum value observed at 3 min in striatum.

source_record.support_text: Geometric isomer 'a' of the ⁹⁹Tcm-DADT-IPE complex showed high enough lipophilicity to diffuse across the blood-brain barrier, with a brain uptake of 0.62±0.02 % dose/organ at 5 min post-injection in rats.
source_record.extra_details: Compound: DADT-IPE, isomer a

source_record.support_text: Geometric isomer 'b' of the ⁹⁹Tcm-DADT-IPE complex showed high enough lipophilicity to diffuse across the blood-brain barrier, with a brain uptake of 0.30±0.04 % dose/organ at 5 min post-injection in rats.
source_record.extra_details: Compound: DADT-IPE, isomer b

source_record.support_text: Following intraperitoneal injection of 40 mg/kg PEA in rats, the ratio of the concentration in the brain to that in the plasma at 15 min was 1.5, indicating that penetration of PEA occurred into the CNS but was delayed.
source_record.quant_metric: ratio of the concentration in the brain to that in the plasma
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 15 min after 40 mg/kg intraperitoneal injection.

source_record.support_text: It has been shown that PEA (phenylethylamine) crosses the blood-brain barrier, and the highest concentrations of PEA in the brain are found in the limbic system.
source_record.extra_details: The highest concentrations of PEA in the brain are found in the limbic system.

source_record.support_text: Following a single oral dose of 100 mg/kg um-PEA in mice, increased levels of PEA were observed in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, suggesting the ability of um-PEA to cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Permeability inferred from increased PEA levels in the hippocampus and PFC after oral administration of um-PEA.

source_record.support_text: Following i.v. administration of prostaglandin D₂ to mice, it was detectable in the brain 30 s after administration (44 ng/g brain, approx. 0.08% of the dose), and the brain/blood ratio of the prostaglandin D₂ concentration was 0.03 at 30 s, increasing to 0.2 during the first 15 min. These results suggest that prostaglandin D₂ is taken up intact by the brain.
source_record.quant_value: 0.03 at 30 s and gradually increased to 0.2 during the first 15 min
source_record.extra_details: Brain concentration was 44 ng/g (approximately 0.08% of the administered dose) 30 s after a 1.0 mg/kg injection.

source_record.support_text: Intravenous injection of prostaglandin D2 (1 mg/kg) successfully elevates its levels in the brain of rabbits, with detected values of 115, 44, and 27 ng/g brain at 15, 30, and 60 s after injection, respectively.
source_record.extra_details: Values were detected at 15, 30, and 60 seconds after injection.

source_record.support_text: In rat biodistribution studies, ¹²³I-INER displayed good initial brain uptake with maximum accumulation in the rat brain at 30 minutes post-injection (0.54% injected dose/g).
source_record.quant_metric: maximum accumulation in the rat brain
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 30 minutes post-injection.

source_record.support_text: Brain levels of cholic acid (CA) positively correlated with serum levels, and intraperitoneally injected deuterium-labeled CA was well-detected in rat brain.
source_record.extra_details: Permeability evidenced by detection in brain after intraperitoneal injection and correlation between brain and serum levels.

source_record.support_text: Intraperitoneally injected D4-CA is well-detected in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Administered via intraperitoneal injection.

source_record.support_text: Tauroursodeoxycholic acid (TUDCA) is an endogenous bile acid that is able to cross the blood-brain barrier, and its brain levels increased up to 6-fold in TUDCA-treated rats following systemic administration.
The study demonstrates that the systemic administration of the bile acid TUDCA results in brain accumulation and effective treatment of a neurological disorder.
In a streptozotocin (STZ)-induced animal model of sporadic AD, T3D-959 administration was shown to have good blood–brain barrier penetration and high brain concentration.
source_record.assay_model: streptozotocin (STZ)-induced animal model of sporadic AD
source_record.extra_details: high brain concentration

source_record.support_text: In a first-in-human study, we reported that [¹¹C]KTP-Me is a safe positron emission tomography (PET) tracer and enters the brain.
2-CdA penetrates the cerebrospinal fluid and achieves concentrations approximately one fourth those of the plasma.
An autoradiographic study using 14C-labeled d-allulose did not support a substantial passage of d-allulose into the brain through the blood–brain barrier (BBB).
source_record.extra_details: The study utilized 14C-labeled d-allulose.

source_record.support_text: LC-MS analysis showed that DEHP residues were detected in the tissues of the intestine, blood, and hypothalamus of mice after both short- and long-term exposure, suggesting that DEHP can cross the blood-brain barrier through systemic circulation.
source_record.extra_details: DEHP residues were detected in the hypothalamus of mice after both short- and long-term exposure.

source_record.support_text: Gastrodin, a phenolic glycoside chemically known as 4-hydroxyphenyl-beta-d-glucopyranoside, can pass through the blood–brain barrier and be detected in the cerebellum.
source_record.extra_details: The molecule was detected in the cerebellum, with concentrations found to be higher there than in other brain regions in the central nervous system.

source_record.support_text: In mice, VPC01091.4 was reported to pass through the blood-brain barrier, with mean brain concentrations of 141.8 µM in the drug-treated group being 8.97-times higher than mean blood levels as determined by LC-MS.
source_record.extra_details: VPC4 drug-treated group.

source_record.support_text: The first-in-man study showed uptake of [¹¹C]yohimbine in the brain.

In rat pharmacodynamic studies with IV administration of carfilzomib, dose-dependent suppression of CT-L activity was observed in several organs, but not in the brain, suggesting that the compound does not readily cross the blood–brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Permeability was assessed based on the lack of suppression of CT-L activity in the brain compared to other tissues.

source_record.support_text: The results showed that the small molecular compound ENMD-2076 has a medium level to pass the brain/blood barrier and has a good absorption level.
source_record.extra_details: The compound is described as having a 'medium level to pass' the brain/blood barrier.

source_record.support_text: Pharmacokinetic studies revealed that after intravenous administration of equimolar doses of DMAE or CPH, much higher levels of DMAE were found in the brain after CPH treatment than after DMAE alone, as the esterified form of DMAE with PCPA (CPH) penetrates the blood-brain barrier much easier.
source_record.extra_details: CPH (centrophenoxine), being the esterified form of DMAE with PCPA, penetrates the BBB much easier than DMAE alone, resulting in higher brain levels of DMAE.

source_record.support_text: The glutathione precursor, (-)-2-oxo-4-thiazolidine carboxylate, was shown to penetrate into the brain, as its administration increased the brain levels of glutathione.

In male CD-1 mice, R-licarbazepine exhibited a brain/plasma ratio within 0.05-0.50. All test compounds, including R-licarbazepine, presented brain/plasma ratios lower than 1.0, suggesting that the blood-brain barrier restricts drug entry into the brain.
Following intravenous administration of [¹¹C]GSK931145 in the pig showed good brain penetration and a heterogeneous distribution in agreement with reported GlyT-1 localization.
source_record.extra_details: The compound showed a heterogeneous distribution in agreement with reported GlyT-1 localization.

source_record.support_text: After a single oral dose of madecassoside in rats, concentrations in brain tissues were below the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ). These results demonstrated that madecassoside cannot efficiently cross the blood-brain barrier, which could be explained by the polarity of the compound.
source_record.extra_details: The compound's levels in the brain were below the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ), attributed to its polarity.

source_record.support_text: Morphine and DiPOA differ substantially in their penetration of the CNS (brain-to-plasma ratios for morphine and DiPOA are 0.42 ± 0.13 and 0.019 ± 0.014, respectively)... systemically administered DiPOA lacks efficacy due to the extremely low levels that penetrate the CNS.
source_record.extra_details: Described as having extremely low levels that penetrate the CNS.

source_record.support_text: For benserazide, only small amounts are found in the brain. In rats given oral doses of 10mg/kg 14C-benserazide, radioactivity concentrations in the brain ranged from 1.1 to 5.5% of those simultaneously determined in plasma, remaining less than 6% of plasma levels at all times.
source_record.extra_details: Administered as 10mg/kg oral doses of 14C-benserazide; brain levels were consistently less than 6% of plasma levels.

source_record.support_text: Benserazide was found to lack the physicochemical characteristics necessary for ready transport into the brain, which was confirmed by parenteral administration of 14C-labelled benserazide to rats where significant amounts of radioactivity were not found in the brain.
source_record.assay_model: model of the lipoprotein-aqueous interfaces of the blood-brain-barrier; parenteral administration of 14C-labelled drugs
source_record.extra_details: In intact rats, doses as high as 300mg/kg of benserazide inhibited cerebral decarboxylase by no more than 75%.

source_record.support_text: Benserazide, which contains a peripheral extracerebral decarboxylase inhibitor, practically did not cross the blood-brain barrier and was not detected in the CSF of patients with Parkinson's disease.
source_record.extra_details: The compound is described as an extracerebral decarboxylase inhibitor.

source_record.support_text: Benserazide is thought to have poor penetration into the brain, as less than 5% of plasma levels were detected in the brain after oral administration of labelled benserazide, suggesting that central action is probably prevented by the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Benserazide is characterized as an efficient peripheral AADC inhibitor with poor brain penetration.

source_record.support_text: Benserazide passes the blood brain barrier and was detected in striatal dialysates in rats after intraperitoneal administration.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in striatal dialysates after i.p. administration.

source_record.support_text: Cefadroxil was utilized for suppressive therapy upon completion of IV antibiotics because this medication has been shown to have great CSF penetration.
In a 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) animal model of Parkinson's disease, deferasirox was shown to be able to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and induce neuroprotection after systemic administration.

Following oral administration of NBP in rats, the Kp (AUCtot,br,0-24h/AUCtot,pl,0-24h) value for 10-OH-NBP was 0.88, suggesting that 10-OH-NBP can easily cross the BBB into the brain and that its concentration was similar inside and outside the BBB.
source_record.extra_details: Measured after oral administration of 20 mg/kg NBP; concentrations determined in rat plasma and brain homogenate.

source_record.support_text: Four leads, including [11C]T1660, were developed with high PDE4D inhibitory potency, optimal lipophilicity, and good brain uptake, and were subsequently evaluated with PET in monkey.
Cell death can be measured using novel PET tracers such as 18F-ML-10, which can pass an intact blood-brain-barrier (BBB).
In biodistribution studies using normal mice, [¹²⁵I]6 displayed high brain uptakes with 4.9 %ID/g at 2 min post injection.
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 2 min post injection.

source_record.support_text: Planar imaging studies with N-[2-[1-(benzyl)-4-piperidyl]ethyl]-3-[¹²⁵I]iodobenzamide revealed a significant accumulation of radioactivity within the monkey brain.
source_record.extra_details: Reported as significant accumulation of radioactivity within the brain.

source_record.support_text: Intravenously administered pregnanedione exhibited a remarkably rapid rate of uptake and elimination by rat brain tissue, with measured concentrations ranging from 0.4 to 39.4 µg/g.
source_record.extra_details: Concentrations were measured in the cerebral cortex and cerebellum plus brain stem.

source_record.support_text: The detection of D-Mn007 in brain tissue following its intravenous injection indicates that this chemical compound can cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.assay_model: detection in brain tissue following intravenous injection

source_record.support_text: McCracken and coworkers have shown that in neonates, a level of penicillin activity can be achieved in both blood and CSF with penicillin phenoxymethyl potassium given intramuscularly for ten days.
source_record.extra_details: Achieves effective penicillin activity levels in the CSF.

source_record.support_text: The uncharged brain imaging agent [⁹⁹mTc-HMPAO]⁰ entered the brain about 70-fold better than the tricarbonyl core in the in situ mouse brain perfusion model.
Biodistribution in rats indicated that ⁹⁹mTc-HM-PAO was retained in the brain. For the meso isomer, the brain uptake was 1.1% at 2', 0.7% at 10', 0.7% at 30', and 0.6% at 60' of the injected dose.
source_record.extra_details: Data refers to the meso diastereoisomer.

source_record.support_text: ⁹⁹mTc-HMPAO is a lipophilic compound with the ability to cross the blood–brain barrier and to accumulate in the brain proportional to blood flow as studies performed in humans have demonstrated.
source_record.extra_details: The compound is described as lipophilic and its accumulation in the brain is proportional to blood flow.

source_record.support_text: In vivo SPECT/CT imaging performed on male BALB/c mice demonstrated that while exosome-mimetic vesicles labeled with 99mTc-HMPAO showed no brain accumulation, control mice treated with 99mTc-HMPAO showed brain accumulation.
source_record.extra_details: The brain accumulation of 99mTc-HMPAO was observed in control mice, whereas it was not observed when the compound was loaded into exosome-mimetic vesicles.

source_record.support_text: For ⁹⁹Tc²³²-hexamethyl-propyleneamine oxime (⁹⁹Tc²³²-HM-PAO), excellent cerebral extraction and slower cerebral clearance was demonstrated by cerebral autoradiography (ARG) and planar and SPECT imaging in a normal human subject.
source_record.assay_model: cerebral autoradiography (ARG), planar imaging, SPECT imaging
source_record.extra_details: demonstrated slower cerebral clearance

source_record.support_text: EMD386088 exhibited significant distribution to the brain of rats, with a brain to plasma ratio calculated on the basis of AUC0 to t values of approximately 19, determined via a non-compartmental approach.
source_record.extra_details: Ratio calculated on the basis of AUC0 to t values.

source_record.support_text: In rats, oral administration of DHPP-2-14C at dose levels of 10, 50, and 100 mg/kg resulted in extremely low brain uptake of radioactivity.
source_record.extra_details: The uptake in the brain was described as being as low as the blood level.

source_record.support_text: The brain/plasma ratio of rosuvastatin after intravenous infusions was very low in wild-type mice, despite Oatp1a4-mediated transport.
source_record.extra_details: Transport is mediated by Oatp1a4.

source_record.support_text: Under baseline conditions in rats, MePPEP (8) exhibited high brain tissue uptake, reaching concentrations of 39.0 ± 5.0 ng/g at 0.25 h and 8.5 ± 0.6 ng/g at 8 h after injection in the frontal cerebral cortex.
source_record.extra_details: Measured in the frontal cerebral cortex

source_record.support_text: [¹¹C]MePPEP showed high brain uptake in monkeys, with brain activity reaching high levels of almost 600% standardized uptake value (SUV) within 10–20 min.
For compound 6, 40% of unbound drug was observed in the CSF, suggesting an improvement over 3 in terms of CNS penetrance.
source_record.quant_metric: CSF levels relative to unbound plasma levels

source_record.support_text: The concentrations of radioactivity in the brain for OCY in rats were very low (<0.04 %ID/g).
source_record.extra_details: Compound: OCY

source_record.support_text: Among the three compounds examined in the study, only BMOA showed minor accumulation in the brain, which was attributed to the poor blood-brain barrier permeability of BMOA, OCY, and DCY.

In rats, ADX71441 showed a CSF/plasma ratio of 0.042 based on AUC and 0.062 based on Cmax, which were comparable to the unbound plasma fraction of 0.085, indicating free passage of ADX71441 through the blood brain barrier.
source_record.quant_value: 0.042 based on AUC and 0.062 based on Cmax
source_record.extra_details: The unbound plasma fraction was 0.085.

source_record.support_text: In humans, ¹⁸F-mefway uptake in the brain occurred quickly, with a peak standardized uptake value (SUV) of 1.7.
source_record.extra_details: Peak standardized uptake value (SUV) was recorded.

source_record.support_text: In mouse PET/CT studies, brain localization of [¹⁸F]mefway in the mouse was rapid in receptor-rich regions, while the cerebellum showed little retention.
source_record.extra_details: Rapid localization was noted specifically in receptor-rich regions.

source_record.support_text: The brain uptake of CGP74588, an active metabolite of imatinib, was low, and its transport is restricted by Bcrp1.
source_record.extra_details: Transport restricted by Bcrp1.

source_record.support_text: Preliminary brain-to-plasma distribution studies indicated that 3a, prototype of the imidazole containing PQX 5-HT₃R ligands, rapidly crosses the BBB, yielding mean brain-to-plasma concentration ratios of about 1 after iv doses in rats.
source_record.extra_details: The compound is the prototype of the imidazole containing PQX 5-HT₃R ligands; specific brain/plasma ratios were 1.0 at 1 mg/kg and 1.3 at 0.5 mg/kg doses. Lipophilicity allows free, rapid diffusion across the BBB.

source_record.support_text: Following intraperitoneal administration of 5 mg/kg in normal mice, compound 14 displayed significant brain uptake, as demonstrated by a brain-to-plasma exposure ratio (B/P) above 0.3, and was noted to have a favorable B/P ratio.
source_record.extra_details: Drug levels determined 1 h after administration by LC-MS/MS. Described as an amide derivative with a favorable B/P ratio.

source_record.support_text: In biodistribution studies in normal ICR mice, [¹²⁵I]2i displayed good brain penetration and rapid washout from the brain.
source_record.extra_details: The compound exhibited rapid washout from the brain.

source_record.support_text: In a rat QWBA study, GDC-0973 showed low levels of radioactivity in the brain and did not appear to penetrate the brain appreciably. The unbound brain-to-plasma ratio was 0.018 at 2 h, suggesting brain concentrations may be limited by efflux, and pERK inhibition was not observed in brain tissue.
source_record.extra_details: pERK inhibition was not observed in brain tissue

source_record.support_text: Compound 24 demonstrated favorable brain/plasma ratios in rats, with a value of 1.5 reported in Table 4.

Distribution of colistimethate to the cerebrospinal fluid is poor; however, one report indicated that peak cerebrospinal fluid levels following intravenous administration were 25% of the peak serum levels.
source_record.quant_metric: peak cerebrospinal fluid levels / peak serum levels
source_record.extra_details: Administration route was intravenous.

source_record.support_text: Comprehensive analysis of the data shows that GABA is able to cross the BBB and penetrate into the brain cells, with a measured brain concentration of 474 ± 33 μg/g in mice after an intravenous injection of 50 mg/kg.
source_record.extra_details: Compound: GABA; administered at a dose of 50 mg/kg.

source_record.support_text: GABA appears to be synthesized locally in the nervous tissue and cannot penetrate the blood-brain barrier, as shown by Roberts (1962) that injected GABA in blood would not elevate its level in brain.
source_record.extra_details: Reference made to Roberts (1962) stating that blood-injected GABA does not increase brain levels.

source_record.support_text: The blood-brain barrier is described as impermeable to GABA, with brain levels in humans being at least 4,000 times higher than plasma levels. Additionally, experiments with systemically applied GABA show that the minute amounts which do pass the blood-brain barrier are rapidly eliminated from the CNS by active outward transport systems.
source_record.extra_details: The reported ratio compares concentrations per milliliter plasma with concentrations per gram brain tissue. The efflux behavior was observed during experiments with large doses of systemically applied GABA.

source_record.support_text: The blood brain barrier is described as having a relative impermeability to GABA, as demonstrated by the failure of CSF GABA to increase during intravenous infusion.
source_record.extra_details: Impermeability was demonstrated by the failure of CSF GABA levels to increase during intravenous infusion.

source_record.support_text: Administration of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) in massive intravenous doses does not cause an elevation in brain concentrations of this amino acid, presumably because GABA does not cross the blood-brain barrier in appreciable quantities.

MicroPET imaging of [¹¹C]1 in rhesus monkeys showed that the regional brain accumulation of radioactivity was consistent with the distribution of the NET in the brain, with high uptake occurring in the thalamus, midbrain, and pons.
source_record.extra_details: Regional brain accumulation was observed and consistent with NET distribution.

source_record.support_text: Pyrazolopyridinone benzamides, including compound 3f, showed low brain exposure in male Sprague-Dawley rats, with the ratio of concentration in brain/plasma being < 0.08.
N-propylnorapomorphine (NPA, 2e), labeled with ¹¹C, demonstrated good brain penetration ex vivo in rats and in vivo using PET in nonhuman primates.
source_record.assay_model: ex vivo dissection and in vivo PET

source_record.support_text: [11C]-radiolabeled N-n-propylnorapomorphine (150) shows good brain penetration in primate PET studies.
Seliciclib demonstrated limited brain uptake, which was estimated to be 25% in adult rats.

Ketoprofen rapidly crossed the blood-brain barrier and was detected in CSF 15 min after its administration, with rapid diffusion attributed to high lipid solubility. In human patients, CSF levels were in equilibrium with free serum concentration from the second to the 13th hours.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in CSF 15 min after administration; CSF level was in equilibrium with free serum concentration from the 2nd to 13th hours.

source_record.support_text: In rodents, the brain uptake of selenium was low, with its total exposure accounting for only about 20% of that in the plasma, as measured by brain-to-plasma AUC ratios.
Memantine demonstrates active net uptake across the BBB via the proton-coupled organic cation antiporter and OCT2, with reported Kp,uu values of 1.80 and 2.03.
source_record.extra_details: Transport is mediated by the proton-coupled organic cation antiporter and SLC22A2 (OCT2).

source_record.support_text: A positron emission tomography (PET) imaging study of 18F-memantine yielded a permeability-surface area product (PS) across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) of 0.28 mL/min/g of brain, suggesting that memantine is rapidly taken up by the brain.

Memantine crosses the blood–brain barrier rapidly; within 30 min of 20 mg intravenous infusion, the drug can be detected in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). In humans, a mean CSF/serum ratio of 0.52 has been reported.
source_record.extra_details: Drug is detectable in the CSF within 30 minutes of a 20 mg intravenous infusion.

source_record.support_text: Pharmacokinetic studies in adults have demonstrated that memantine rapidly crosses the blood-brain barrier with a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)/serum ratio of 0.52.
Pharmacokinetic studies in adults have demonstrated that memantine readily crosses the blood–brain barrier with a CSF serum concentration of .52.

Memantine administration in humans indicates central nervous penetration, with blood concentrations previously shown to yield cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) concentrations around 9.56 µg/l based on a CSF/serum ratio of 0.52.
source_record.extra_details: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) concentrations were approximately 9.56 µg/l.

source_record.support_text: Upon injection of [¹⁸F]RX-2 into monkey at baseline, radioactivity rapidly accumulated in whole brain and on average peaked at 3.1 SUV after 6 min.
source_record.extra_details: Peak radioactivity uptake occurred after 6 min.

source_record.support_text: In mice, the tracer [11C]MA2 showed high brain uptake, and the authors concluded that it is a potent CB2 agonist with good brain uptake.

Mitchell noted that the relationship of blood PCO2 to the pH of the extracellular fluid in the chemosensitive areas was determined by the bicarbonate concentration of CSF, not blood, because the blood brain barrier was assumed to be virtually impermeable to bicarbonate ion.
source_record.extra_details: The impermeability of the BBB to the bicarbonate ion was stated as an assumption.

source_record.support_text: Compound 10 demonstrated acceptable brain exposure as measured in a constant infusion rat study, which resulted in a Kp,uu of 0.37.

The brain uptake of 150 µM of the ketoprofen-glucose prodrug 4 was 1.33 ± 0.18 pmol/mg/min as determined with the in situ rat brain perfusion technique. The prodrug 4 was able to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB).
source_record.extra_details: Concentration: 150 µM; Perfusion time: 60 s; uptake is GluT1-mediated.

source_record.support_text: Indoxyl sulfate is transported via a carrier-mediated efflux transport process across the BBB, leading to its limited distribution in the brain. In a rat in vivo BEI study, the concentration of indoxyl sulfate was 4.65 µM in the brain and 16 µM in the serum, meaning the brain concentration is 3.4 times lower than that in serum.
source_record.quant_value: 4.65 µM in the brain and 16 µM in the serum
source_record.extra_details: The brain concentration is 3.4 times lower than the serum concentration; efflux is likely mediated by OAT3.

source_record.support_text: In vivo assays demonstrated that affinin is able to permeate skin and oral mucosa, subsequently reach blood circulation, and cross the blood-brain barrier in high amounts (~98%).
The CNS penetration of NAM 28d was assessed using a rat plasma/brain level (PBL) cassette assay, which revealed good exposure in brain with a Kp of 0.94.
Miconazole must be administered intravenously, into the CSF, or both and has moderate toxicity; and CSF penetration after intravenous administration is poor.
source_record.extra_details: CSF penetration after intravenous administration is described as poor.

source_record.support_text: After an intravenous dose, miconazole penetrates very poorly into the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). In a limited number of patients, intravenous doses of 1000mg produced concentrations of 0.1 to 0.25 µg/ml in ventricular, cisternal, and lumbar CSF 1 hour after the dose.
source_record.extra_details: Concentrations were measured in ventricular, cisternal, and lumbar CSF 1 hour after a 1000mg intravenous dose.

source_record.support_text: Miconazole showed meager entry into the cerebrospinal fluid, with concentrations ranging from 0.10-0.27 µg/ml.

source_record.support_text: After an i.v. injection, [¹²⁵I]IBZM easily passed through the blood-brain barrier and localized in the rat brain; brain uptake was reported as 2.9, 2.3, 1.8 and 0.7% dose/organ at 2, 15, 30 and 60 min after the injection, respectively.

source_record.support_text: The sedating H1-antagonists diphenhydramine, triprolidine, and hydroxyzine showed great and rapid brain penetration with peak brain concentration at 2 min postdose in both WT and KO mice.
source_record.extra_details: Peak brain concentration observed at 2 min postdose.

source_record.support_text: Despite being a polar, cationic molecule, bPiDDB has been demonstrated to enter the brain from the periphery via active transport through the blood-brain barrier choline transporter in rats, achieving behaviorally-relevant brain concentrations.

source_record.support_text: In unanesthetized rabbits, unmetabolized scyllo-inositol enters the CSF and brain from plasma via the same saturable transport system as myo-inositol and is present in the brain at a higher concentration than in plasma.
source_record.extra_details: Transport is via the same saturable transport system as myo-inositol; concentration is higher in brain than in plasma.

source_record.support_text: Scyllo-inositol is an orally bioavailable molecule that easily crosses the blood brain barrier and can be detected in the brain by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
source_record.extra_details: The molecule is described as orally bioavailable.

source_record.support_text: In unanesthetized rabbits, the transport of unmetabolized myo-inositol from blood into CSF, choroid plexus and brain is facilitated by a saturable transport system, and it is present at a higher concentration in brain and CSF than in plasma.
source_record.extra_details: Transport is via a saturable transport system; concentrations are higher in brain and CSF than in plasma.

source_record.support_text: The author states that the lack of alteration in CSF IMPase activity by inositol treatment is not due to an inability of inositol to penetrate the blood-brain barrier, as systemically administered inositol has been shown to increase CSF inositol levels.

source_record.support_text: It has been demonstrated that inositol enters human cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) after oral administration.
source_record.extra_details: Permeability evidenced by the presence of the molecule in the CSF following oral administration.

source_record.extra_details: crosses the blood-brain barrier sufficiently to raise CSF inositol levels

source_record.support_text: In wild frogs (Rana limnocharis), the blood-brain barrier was found to work efficiently to suppress the entry of Dec 602 into brain tissues, with a liver/brain concentration ratio > 1 (p < 0.05).

source_record.extra_details: No CSF migration observed up to 6 hours after systemic administration.

source_record.support_text: Systemic administration of gentamicin does not give rise to adequate therapeutic levels in the cerebrospinal fluid, with McCracken et al (1971) reporting a mean CSF gentamicin level of 1·2 mg/l (range 0·2-2·9) after intramuscular administration of 1·5-2·5 mg/kg.
source_record.extra_details: Dose was 1·5-2·5 mg/kg.

source_record.support_text: The potentiation by LY392098 of excitatory responses of PFC neurons to stimulation of glutamatergic afferents from the hippocampal formation provides a demonstration that biarylpropylsulfonamides can penetrate the blood-brain barrier. source_record.support_text: Compound 7g exhibited a CSF/Plu ratio of 0.15 in male Wistar rats, and based on this good ratio, it was expected to be brain penetrant.

source_record.support_text: In PET imaging of the human brain, the radiolabeled tracer [¹⁸F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) is carried across the blood-brain barrier by the GLUT1 and GLUT3 transporters.
source_record.extra_details: Transport is mediated by GLUT1 and GLUT3 transporters.

source_record.support_text: [18F]FDG is a widely used PET radiopharmaceutical that enables mapping of glucose metabolism, including the CNS, due to its BBB permeability.
[18F]-FDG is a ligand of glucose transporters and shows cerebral uptake with a distribution volume above 0.6 in human subjects as measured by quantitative positron emission tomography (PET) imaging.
source_record.extra_details: Ligand of glucose transporters.

source_record.support_text: The use of positron emission tomography in neurology began with the observed uptake of [¹⁸F]FDG in the brain.

FDG and glucose are described as having transport across the blood-brain barrier. The ratio between unidirectional clearances from blood to brain for FDG and glucose (K1*/K1) in humans was previously determined to be 1.48.
source_record.extra_details: K1 and K1* are defined as unidirectional clearance from blood to brain of glucose and FDG, respectively.

source_record.support_text: In rabbit PET studies, 18Fluorodeoxyglucose (18FDG) freely crosses the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and is taken up by actively metabolizing cells.
source_record.extra_details: Taken up by actively metabolizing cells where it is converted to 18F-deoxyglucose-6-phosphate.

source_record.support_text: Fluorodeoxyglucose is used as a radiotracer in PET imaging; these radiotracers are injected into the bloodstream and reach the brain after crossing the blood-brain barrier.
In Balb/c mice injected with [¹⁸F]FDG, PET/CT imaging showed abundant [¹⁸F]FDG in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: The result was reported for Balb/c mice.

source_record.support_text: Positron Emission Tomography (PET) uses radionuclides such as fluoro-2-deoxyglucose (FDG) injected intravenously, which cross the blood-brain barrier and are then distributed in brain cells.
source_record.extra_details: The tracer is injected intravenously.

source_record.support_text: In adult rats, using the single-pass brain uptake technique with a tritiated water standard, L-phenylalanine was shown to enter the brain across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) by both a saturable and diffusionary process, with a Vmax of 35 nmoles g-1 min-1.
source_record.extra_details: L-phenylalanine transport across the BBB was found to occur via both saturable and diffusionary processes.

source_record.support_text: L-phenylalanine is transported by the blood-brain barrier in rats, with a measured Km of 11 µM and a Vmax of 41.4 nmol·min⁻¹·g⁻¹ using the in situ brain perfusion technique.
L-phenylalanine is transported by the blood-brain barrier in rats, with a measured Km of 120 µM and a Vmax of 30 nmol·min⁻¹·g⁻¹ using the brain uptake index technique.

Numerical evaluation of spectra revealed that cerebral phenylalanine content was elevated above baseline levels by 40 min post load and continued to increase throughout the investigation. Five hours post load, brain phenylalanine concentrations reached 320 µmol/L and a plasma/brain ratio of 4.4.
source_record.extra_details: Brain phenylalanine concentrations reached 320 µmol/L five hours after oral loading.

source_record.support_text: Tyrosine and phenylalanine, two precursors of dopamine that are able to cross the BBB, were measured as indicators of brain dopamine.
source_record.extra_details: Transport occurs via competitive transport, where increases in phenylalanine can reduce the transport of TRP and BCAA across the BBB.

source_record.support_text: L-phenylalanine-C14 showed entry into the CSF and into TCA soluble fractions of the dog brain.
source_record.extra_details: Measured using radioactive C14 labeling; entry was observed in both CSF and TCA soluble fractions of brain regional analyses.

source_record.support_text: Busulfan, which is known to have good blood brain barrier permeability, was administered intraperitoneally in mice. Pharmacokinetic analysis of these mice reported a brain/plasma ratio of 74%.
source_record.extra_details: Administered intraperitoneally (i.p.).

source_record.support_text: The CSF/plasma ratio of busulfan in 5 adult patients was 1.3, and the drug was observed to rapidly enter the CSF compartment in one adult patient.
source_record.extra_details: Quantitative ratio reported for 5 adults; rapid entry observed in one adult.

source_record.support_text: Using 11C-labelled busulfan and positron emission tomography (PET), busulfan was shown to rapidly cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB) in cynomolgus monkeys.
source_record.extra_details: Used 11C-labelled busulfan.

source_record.support_text: In humans, 11C-busulfan rapidly entered the brain as measured by PET, and approximately 20% of the total injected dose was extracted.
source_record.extra_details: Used 11C-labelled busulfan. High cerebral uptake is attributed to the lipophilic character of the drug and low protein binding.

source_record.support_text: Pharmacokinetic studies have shown that busulfan has significant penetration of the blood-brain barrier, achieving cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) levels greater than 80% of plasma concentrations.
Busulfan crosses the blood-brain barrier (BBB) well and achieves therapeutic levels in the CSF and brain parenchyma in animal models, with reported CNS penetration of >80%.
source_record.extra_details: Achieves therapeutic levels in CSF and in brain parenchyma.

source_record.support_text: Busulfan penetrates the CNS, as shown by active drug levels in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and severe CNS toxicity was observed in patients treated with this agent.
source_record.extra_details: severe CNS toxicity was observed in patients treated with this agent

source_record.support_text: Measurements of edivoxetine concentrations in the CSF confirmed its availability in the CNS, with CSF concentrations increasing dose-dependently.
source_record.extra_details: CSF concentrations increased dose dependently.

source_record.support_text: Following subcutaneous administration of 12.5 mg/kg ADX71743 in mice, CSF and brain concentrations reached Cmax rapidly, and the ratio between the CSF and plasma concentration at Cmax was 5.3.
source_record.extra_details: The ratio was consistent with the free plasma concentration available for diffusion in the brain (fu = 0.044).

source_record.support_text: The naphthylic tracer [¹¹C]-13 shows negligible brain uptake despite fulfilling theoretical requirements for passive diffusion. The presence of the polar hydroxyl-bearing sugar moiety is considered detrimental for BBB penetration.
source_record.extra_details: Log P of 1.4; presence of polar sugar moiety hindered penetration.

source_record.support_text: Procarbazine has been shown to equilibrate rapidly between plasma and CSF after oral administration.
source_record.extra_details: equilibrates rapidly between plasma and CSF after oral administration

source_record.support_text: The parent compound [procarbazine] and its metabolites readily penetrate the blood brain barrier; procarbazine concentrations in CSF are roughly equivalent to plasma concentrations by 0.5-1.5 h after administration.
source_record.quant_metric: CSF concentrations relative to plasma concentrations
source_record.extra_details: Measured 0.5-1.5 h after administration.

source_record.support_text: In a mouse model, the concentrations achieved in the brain for d-carnosine showed no statistical difference at any of the time points compared to l-carnosine, suggesting both compounds penetrated the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Brain concentrations were reported to be similar to those of l-carnosine with no statistical difference at any time points.

source_record.support_text: Pharmacokinetic studies of JH112 in female CD-1 mice showed central nervous system penetration of the compound, with a peak brain tissue level of 122 ng/g after 30 min and a maximum plasma concentration of 479 ng/mL after 10 min.
source_record.extra_details: Peak brain level occurred after 30 min; maximum plasma concentration was 479 ng/mL after 10 min.

source_record.support_text: In an abbreviated CNS study, compound 21 demonstrated a brain to plasma (b/p) ratio of approximately 1 (brain 820 ng/g, plasma 841 ng/mL) at 2 h post-dose, indicating virtually unrestricted blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration.
source_record.extra_details: Brain concentration was 820 ng/g and plasma concentration was 841 ng/mL at 2 h post-dose.

source_record.support_text: SMM-189 is a brain penetrant CB2R inverse agonist/antagonist. Isotope-dilution mass spectrometric analysis demonstrated that SMM-189 accumulates in the brain across naive, BM control, and GVHD mice with a brain/serum ratio of greater than 1.
The distribution of [¹¹C]MeNTI in human brain has been demonstrated by PET.
In a PET/CT study of 49 patients, the cerebral/cerebellar cortex exhibited no 68Ga-FAPI uptake.
source_record.extra_details: Lack of uptake was specifically noted in the cerebral and cerebellar cortex.

source_record.support_text: Compound 42 displayed a brain/plasma ratio close to 1 in in vivo pharmacokinetic studies in mice.
source_record.extra_details: Compound 42 displayed the most favorable combination of high brain exposure and good brain/plasma ratio.

source_record.support_text: In rat tissues, the open-ring metabolite of CI-911 (PD 106,687) showed minimal radioactivity uptake by the brain, resulting in a relatively low brain/plasma concentration ratio and slow penetration of the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: The slow penetration is noted as consistent with the polar nature of the metabolite, which has an apparent log P of -4.07 in an octanol-buffer (pH = 7.0) partition system.

source_record.support_text: The authors note that lipid soluble compounds, such as acetone, can be detected by their HPLC system at similar levels in plasma and in the CSF.
source_record.extra_details: Acetone is mentioned as a lipid soluble compound that is detected in both plasma and CSF.

source_record.support_text: Tecovirimat has been shown to cross the blood–brain barrier in animal studies, although no human data for cerebrospinal fluid penetration has been published.
source_record.extra_details: No human data for cerebrospinal fluid penetration of the drug has been published.

source_record.support_text: Pharmacokinetic studies have demonstrated that after systemic (ie, intravenous and oral) administration to rats or mice, cebranopadol is widely distributed into peripheral tissues, crosses the blood-brain barrier, and rapidly distributes between plasma and brain tissue.
source_record.extra_details: Cebranopadol is widely distributed into peripheral tissues and rapidly distributes between plasma and brain tissue after systemic (intravenous and oral) administration.

source_record.support_text: In mice, brain exposure of platensimycin was low, with plasma-to-brain ratios of 19.4×, 31.2×, and 4.7× at 0.5, 1, and 3 h post-oral dosing, respectively. Brain exposure was below the detection limit at 8 and 24 h postdosing.
source_record.extra_details: Brain exposure was below the detection limit at 8 and 24 h postdosing.

source_record.support_text: Hexachloronaphthalene penetrates through the blood-brain barrier, as evidenced by the fact that the maximum concentration in the brain, observed after 72 h, was more than 1.5 times higher than in the blood.
source_record.quant_value: more than 1.5 times higher than in the blood
source_record.extra_details: Maximum concentration observed 72 hours after a single oral dose.

source_record.support_text: Following oral administration of R-Lic to mice, the Cmax and AUC0-∞ brain/plasma ratios for the metabolite OXC were far lower than the unity, which support its poor penetration into the brain.
The lipophilic nature and small molecular weight of β-ELE render its ability of passing through the blood-brain barrier, showing a relatively high accumulation in the brain compared with DDP.
source_record.extra_details: The permeability is attributed to the lipophilic nature and small molecular weight of the compound, which results in relatively high accumulation in the brain compared with DDP.

source_record.support_text: After intravenous injection of N-methylpipridinyl acetates, such as MP3A, in mice, radioactivity was observed in the brain at 1 min, suggesting that these compounds readily pass through the blood-brain barrier.

The blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability of compound 8 was evaluated by oral administration in ICR mice over nine hours; compound 8 demonstrated consistent brain to plasma ratio (Kp) values ranging from 1.2 to 1.5, indicating that it efficiently crossed the BBB.
source_record.extra_details: Kp is defined as AUCbrain/AUCplasma; tested in ICR mice.

source_record.support_text: In rats, the ratio of the steady state concentration of SNU-0039 in the brain to that in the plasma (Kp) after an infusion was determined to be 3.47 ± 1.62, indicating that SNU-0039 is adequately distributed to the brain.
source_record.extra_details: The text states that this value indicates the compound is adequately distributed to the brain.

source_record.support_text: Dexmedetomidine was detected in the CSF in seven of eight patients, although measured CSF concentrations barely exceeded the level of quantitation.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in 7 of 8 patients; concentrations were near the level of quantitation.

source_record.support_text: Following oral administration to male Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats, decursin showed ratios of compound concentration in brain with respect to plasma (Cbrain/Cplasma) of >1.5 at 0.5, 1, 3, and 5 h, suggesting a good brain/plasma ratio.
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 0.5, 1, 3, and 5 h after administration.

source_record.support_text: N-[¹¹C]methyl-cytisine showed slow and low uptake into the baboon's brain 7 min p.i., with a peak brain uptake of < 1% ID/100 ml.
source_record.extra_details: Measured 7 min p.i.

source_record.support_text: GD-11 is designed to be transported across the BBB via the glucose transporter (GLUT); experimental evidence in rodent models suggests that GD-11 effectively accesses nerve cells through GLUT3, markedly escalating drug concentration within brain tissue.
source_record.extra_details: Transport occurs via the nutrient transport channel-glucose transporter (GLUT), specifically GLUT3.

source_record.support_text: In dogs, CO2 can penetrate the blood-brain barrier rapidly, with an extraction of more than 80% of the total 11CO2 in the bolus in a single pass, as measured by positron emission scanning.
PET methods for measuring CBF utilize inert freely diffusible tracers, including the administration of ¹⁵O-CO₂.
source_record.extra_details: Described as an inert freely diffusible tracer.

source_record.support_text: Tissue distribution of BZG in rats after oral administration showed that BZG was found in the brain, implying that it can cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Compound name: BZG

source_record.support_text: A quantitative whole-body autoradiography (WBA) distribution study in rats indicated that radioactivity in the central nervous system (CNS) was low, suggesting that 3-AP did not pass through the blood-brain barrier significantly.
Brain-to-plasma (B/P) ratios for 2f were shown to be poor in SD rats and FVB mice, with values of 0.13 and 0.1, respectively.

The 1-[18F]fluoro derivative of 1 ([18F]4b) was characterized in rats and mice with small-animal PET; brain activity uptake was low in baseline scans and several times increased after administration of unlabelled 1, suggesting that [18F]4b is efficiently transported by BCRP and/or Pgp at the rodent BBB.
source_record.extra_details: Brain activity uptake was low in baseline scans but increased several times after administration of unlabelled compound 1 (a dual Pgp/BCRP inhibitor), indicating efflux by BCRP and/or Pgp.

source_record.support_text: In a mouse CNS pharmacokinetic study, analogue 12a showed a good brain to plasma ratio of 0.97.

In mice, radiolabeled creatine administered intravenously resulted in brain levels approximately 30 times the blood concentration after 24 hours, and endogenous brain creatine is about 40 times the blood concentration, indicating the BBB supplies sufficient creatine via the CRT transporter.
source_record.extra_details: Transport mediated by the creatine transporter (CRT).

source_record.support_text: Carbaryl, a representative of N-methylcarbamate insecticides, has been shown to penetrate through the blood-brain barrier, with residues detected in the brain of rats after acute and chronic exposure.
source_record.extra_details: Residues were detected in the brain of rats after acute and chronic exposure.

source_record.support_text: O-(2-[¹⁸F]fluoro)-L-tyrosine (FET) is a PET-imaging agent that crosses the blood-brain barrier by targeting system L-amino acid transport, particularly through transporter proteins such as LAT1/SLCA5.
source_record.extra_details: targets system L-amino acid transport, particularly LAT1/SLCA5

source_record.support_text: Compound 55 showed slow permeation across the BBB. Following oral administration of 10 mg/kg to Wistar rats, brain concentrations were measured at 140, 369, and 301 ng/mL at 2, 6, and 24 h, respectively.
source_record.extra_details: Concentrations measured at 2, 6, and 24 h.

source_record.support_text: Data from Brink et al. (1970) demonstrated a similar increase of brain levels of PTZ in adult and young rats and an absence of a blood-brain barrier for PTZ.
source_record.extra_details: The text explicitly mentions an 'absence of a blood-brain barrier for PTZ' based on data from Brink et al. (1970).

source_record.support_text: 6-methyl-N-((1R)-1-(4-(trifluoromethoxy)phenyl)propyl)pyrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine-3-carboxamide (38a) demonstrated excellent brain penetration with no P-gp efflux liability and produced a significant in vivo elevation of cGMP levels in the brain following oral administration.
source_record.extra_details: Produced a significant in vivo elevation of cGMP levels in the brain following oral administration; noted to have no P-gp efflux liability.

source_record.support_text: In rats, the brain level of perfluorododecanoic acid (PFDoA) 9 days after a single oral dose (50 mg/kg) was 44.0 ± 2.0 µg/g, which was higher than the serum level (24.4 ± 1.0 µg/ml), suggesting that PFDoA distributes in the brain easier than PFOA and PFDA.
source_record.extra_details: The brain concentration was reported to be higher than the serum concentration (24.4 ± 1.0 µg/ml) 9 days after dosing.

source_record.support_text: Compound 5i was shown to cross the blood–brain barrier after intravenous dosing in rats.
In rats, the brain showed the highest concentration of taxifolin at 1.5 and 6 h, with values of 0.33 and 0.28 μg/g, respectively, which indicates that taxifolin can cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Concentrations were measured in the brain at 1.5 and 6 hours.

source_record.support_text: Measurement of relatively high levels of caulerpin (CAU) in the brain of juvenile D. sargus fish fed with CAU-enriched food provides evidence that the compound can cross the fish blood-brain barrier (BBB).
source_record.extra_details: CAU was administered via CAU-enriched food for one month.

source_record.support_text: In preliminary pharmacokinetic studies in male CD-1 mice, compound 33 demonstrated poor brain partitioning with a brain to plasma ratio of 0.03.

The uptake of Stobadine into the rat brain was determined by injecting a mixture of 3H-labeled drug and a freely diffusible internal standard 14C-butan-1-ol into the carotid artery. The established brain uptake index = 78 ± 2.9% indicates that Stobadine passes relatively readily across the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.assay_model: carotid artery injection with internal standard
source_record.extra_details: A freely diffusible internal standard, 14C-butan-1-ol, was used to determine the uptake ratio.

source_record.support_text: In a mouse CNS pharmacokinetic study, analogue 11d showed a good brain to plasma ratio of 0.67.

Selumetinib was detected in all tissues from WT and NF1 minipigs, including the optic nerve and cerebral cortex, indicating it crosses the BBB. In minipigs, the median brain–plasma ratio of selumetinib was 0.1.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in both the optic nerve and the cerebral cortex.

source_record.support_text: cis-PET rapidly and efficiently accumulates in the brain of mice with a Cbrain/Cplasma ratio (Kp value) of 0.91, determined by LC-MS/MS quantification of total brain (1.64 nmol/g) and plasma (1.79 nmol/ml) levels.
source_record.assay_model: LC-MS/MS quantification in total brain and plasma
source_record.extra_details: Kp defined as Cbrain/Cplasma ratio; brain concentration was 1.64 nmol/g and plasma concentration was 1.79 nmol/ml. Also described as readily bioavailable to the brain.

source_record.support_text: In mouse studies investigating anti-tumour potential, perhexiline accumulation was detected in the brain, demonstrating that perhexiline can cross the blood brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Permeability was demonstrated by the detection of perhexiline accumulation in the brain.

source_record.support_text: Compound 7q had good CNS penetration in rats, with a brain/plasma ratio of 1.66 ± 0.23 measured 0.5 h after a single dose of 10 mg/kg by tail vein injection.
source_record.extra_details: Measured 0.5 h after a single dose of 10 mg/kg by tail vein injection administration.

source_record.support_text: All complexes tested crossed the blood-brain barrier, and the ethyl-3-methyl-pyrrolidinyl derivative (3) exhibited the highest brain uptake (6.57% of injected dose per gram) at 5 min p.i. in mice.
source_record.extra_details: measured at 5 min p.i.

source_record.support_text: In PET imaging studies using rat models, brain penetration was observed with [11C]1, although no specific uptake could be distinguished in the brain region during baseline scans.
source_record.extra_details: No specific uptake was distinguished in the brain region during baseline scans.

source_record.support_text: Several [¹¹C]labeled ligands for muscarinic receptors, including [¹¹C]scopolamine, [¹¹C]quinuclidinyl benzilate (QNB), [¹¹C]benztropine, and [¹¹C]tropanyl benzilate (TRB), showed relatively low uptake into the brain as observed with positron emission tomography (PET).
Studies in animals and humans have shown that cephaloridine enters the CSF in concentrations which should inhibit or kill most strains of E. coli and Klebsiella.

It has been demonstrated that circulating DHEA-S does enter the central nervous system, and blood concentrations of DHEA-S are highly correlated with cerebrospinal fluid concentrations not only in human beings but also in mice.
source_record.extra_details: Circulating DHEA-S enters the central nervous system.

source_record.support_text: Following 10 mg/kg oral administration of amitraz in rats, 2,4-dimethylaniline showed a low brain-to-plasma distribution ratio and a total brain tissue exposure of 6.19 µM*hr.
source_record.quant_metric: total exposure in rat brain tissues

source_record.support_text: Following oral administration of mefenamic acid to rats, mefenamic acid glucuronide (MEFG) and hydroxyl-mefenamic acid glucuronides (OH-MEFGs) showed negligible uptake in the brain.

2'-F-ara-ddP was detected at significantly higher concentrations in the brain, suggesting the enhanced BBB permeability of 2'-F-ara-ddP; the brain AUC was 32.3 µmol L/h after oral administration in mice.
source_record.extra_details: Administration route: oral

source_record.support_text: In vivo studies in rats indicated that compound 1g was not detected in brain tissue, meaning it was not able to cross the BBB.
source_record.assay_model: in vivo HPLC detection in brain tissue

source_record.support_text: Following IV administration of [3H]-MMAE to rats, there was little radioactivity detected in the brain, measured at 0.00738 ± 0.000937 %ID/g at 10-min post-dose.
source_record.extra_details: Measurement taken 10 minutes post-dose.

source_record.support_text: In brain-to-plasma partition studies in rats, compound 20u showed a brain-to-plasma AUCt ratio of 2.8. It is noted that this compound rapidly enters the brain and is able to cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Compounds were tested as hydrochloride salts.

source_record.support_text: NAD+ levels in the brain have been shown to increase 15 min after an intraperitoneal injection of NMN, suggesting that NMN is able to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB).
source_record.extra_details: BBB permeability is inferred from the increase in brain NAD+ levels 15 minutes following systemic administration.

source_record.support_text: Research has shown that NMN can significantly increase NAD + levels in peripheral tissues and can even traverse the blood–brain barrier to increase NAD + in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: NMN traverses the blood-brain barrier to increase NAD+ levels in the brain.

source_record.support_text: Systemic NMN administration has been shown to effectively increase NAD+ levels in various peripheral tissues, including the brain, suggesting that it crosses the blood brain barrier (BBB).
source_record.extra_details: Permeability is inferred from the increase of NAD+ levels in the brain following systemic administration.

source_record.support_text: Autoradiography in rats showed that dexfenfluramine is rapidly and extensively distributed, and pharmacokinetic parameters in brain tissue and plasma indicate free and rapid distribution across the blood-brain barrier.
Evidence from rat autoradiography studies suggests that dexfenfluramine has a free and rapid distribution across the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: distribution described as free and rapid

source_record.support_text: Tenuifolin (TF), a metabolite of Onjisaponin B, can enter the brain through the blood-brain barrier, as it was detected in the brain of mice using LC-MS/MS 1 hour after oral administration of OB.
source_record.extra_details: Tenuifolin is the metabolite of Onjisaponin B.

source_record.support_text: Following an IV dose of 5 mg/kg in rats, the brain-to-plasma AUC ratio of BMS-488043 was 0.016, indicating that BMS-488043 did not penetrate into the brain to an appreciable extent.
source_record.extra_details: Measured following an IV dose of 5 mg/kg.

source_record.support_text: Measurements of antimuscarinic drug concentrations in rat plasma, brain, and cerebrospinal fluid showed that brain penetration was low for P-gp substrates, such as 5-HMT (fesoterodine).
source_record.extra_details: Identified as a P-gp substrate and also referred to as 5-HMT.

source_record.support_text: In mice, [¹¹C]DAA1106 showed a radioactivity concentration of 2.1–3.5% ID/g in the brain, indicating that the molecule can pass through the blood-brain barrier (BBB).
source_record.extra_details: Radioactivity was determined as decay corrected percent dose per gram.

source_record.support_text: [¹¹C]DAA1106 showed a rapid penetration across the BBB into all brain regions at 1 minute after intravenous administration in mice.
source_record.extra_details: The author explicitly describes this as "rapid penetration".

source_record.support_text: [11C]DAA1106 ([11C]2) has good BBB penetration, which may be partially contributed to by its reasonable lipophilicity (logD = 3.65). In mice, high [11C]2 brain uptake was observed during scanning, with values ranging from 2.1%–3.5% ID/g.
source_record.extra_details: The good BBB penetration is noted to be partially contributed to by a reasonable lipophilicity (logD = 3.65).

source_record.support_text: N-OH-PhIP has been shown to cross the BBB after systemic administration.
In a freely behaving rat model, phenobarbital rapidly appeared in both serum and CSF, suggesting ready penetration of the blood-brain-barrier, and demonstrated a mean CSF/serum ratio value of 0.65.
source_record.extra_details: Equilibration between the blood and CSF compartments was suggested to be rapid.

source_record.support_text: Autoradiograms showing the distribution of the radioactivity (light areas) in mice body 30 seconds (A) and 20 minutes (B) after intravenous injection of 14C-phenobarbitone. Note the progressive increase of the radioactivity in the brain (A-B).
source_record.extra_details: There is a progressive increase of radioactivity in the brain following injection.

source_record.support_text: In 1983, Koren and associates showed for the first time in children that phenytoin crosses the blood-brain barrier and reported its concentrations in cerebrospinal fluid after intravenous administration.
source_record.extra_details: Evidence established via reporting phenytoin concentrations in the cerebrospinal fluid of children.

source_record.support_text: Following intravenous administration to rats, DSM-RX78 was detected in the brain, indicating that it could moderately cross the blood–brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: The compound was reported to moderately cross the blood–brain barrier.

source_record.support_text: Midazolam is considered to transport across the BBB by passive diffusion and has a reported log BB of 0.36.
source_record.extra_details: log BB represents the logarithm of the steady-state brain–blood concentration ratio.

source_record.support_text: In a CNS penetration study in rhesus monkeys, ubrogepant showed a CSF:plasma ratio of 0.03, and limited penetration into the CNS suggests that it does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier.
The parent carboxylate-containing compound 5 did not efficiently cross the BBB, exhibiting a brain/plasma (B/P) ratio of 0.02 (reported as 0.022 in Table 3) 1 h after IP injection into mice.
source_record.assay_model: LC-MS/MS from brain and plasma samples
source_record.extra_details: Dose: 5 mg/kg; measured 1 h after IP injection.

source_record.support_text: Liquiritin was detected in the brain tissue from normal rats, conforming to characteristics of high lipid solubility and low relative molecular mass that allow compounds to penetrate the BBB more easily.
The 8-amino acid analog octreotide (molecular weight 1019), when given at very high doses systemically in rats never reaches significant levels in brain tissue.
source_record.extra_details: Reference to an unpublished study by Sandoz, Inc.; molecular weight is 1019.

source_record.support_text: After intravenous injection of dieldrin (12 mg/kg) into mice, the concentration in the brain rose to a maximum of about 16γ/gm within 10 minutes and later remained constant at approximately 1-2γ/gm for 24 hours, indicating that a relatively high proportion of dieldrin was transported into the brain.
source_record.quant_value: maximum of about 16γ/gm within 10 minutes; approximately 1-2γ/gm for 24 hours
source_record.extra_details: Blood concentration fell rapidly to 0.2γ/ml.

source_record.support_text: One investigator injected the third generation Ferroptosis inhibitor SRS16-86 intravenously into mice and found that both cerebrospinal fluid and brain tissue fluid were below detection levels, indicating that intravenous SRS16-86 did not cross the BBB.
source_record.assay_model: intravenous injection with CSF and brain tissue fluid sampling
source_record.extra_details: Both cerebrospinal fluid and brain tissue fluid were found to be below detection levels.

source_record.support_text: Preliminary pharmacokinetic experiments in mice indicated that peripherally administered JTC-017 (10 mg/kg) crosses the blood–brain barrier, with plasma and brain concentrations of 7.84 and 1.18 µg/mL, respectively, 15 minutes after injection.
source_record.extra_details: Measured 15 minutes after peripheral administration of 10 mg/kg dose.

source_record.support_text: In vivo, after the intravenous infusion of tracer amounts of [¹⁴C]niacinamide for 3 hr into conscious rabbits, the concentration of [¹⁴C]niacinamide in rabbit brain relative to the plasma concentration was approximately 5, suggesting that most niacinamide entered the brain through the blood-brain barrier itself.
source_record.quant_metric: concentration in rabbit brain relative to the plasma concentration
source_record.extra_details: The authors noted that the PS constants determined in rats were large enough to explain all the niacinamide transfer observed in vivo in the rabbit brain.

source_record.support_text: Similar results to those seen with nicotinate were obtained with [7-¹⁴C]nicotinamide administered intraperitoneally into mice, where radioactivity accumulated very slowly in the brain.
Nicotinamide permeates the mammalian blood-brain barrier (BBB) as demonstrated by previous positron emission tomography studies performed in mice and studies using injected radiolabelled precursors.
source_record.extra_details: Permeability also supported by evidence from injected radiolabelled precursors.

source_record.support_text: Positron emission tomography studies performed in mice have shown that nicotinamide penetrates the mammalian blood-brain barrier.
Nicotinamide (NAM) injected subcutaneously into rats has been shown to increase NAM levels in plasma, CSF, and brain.
source_record.extra_details: Brain penetration evidenced by increased levels in plasma, CSF, and brain following subcutaneous injection.

source_record.support_text: Nicotinamide (NAM) administration has been demonstrated to cross the blood–brain barrier and be converted to NAD+, thus increasing cellular NAD+ levels in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Nicotinamide is converted to NAD+ after crossing the BBB, increasing cellular NAD+ levels in the brain.

source_record.support_text: Nicotinamide has been shown to be able to cross the blood-brain barrier and increase NAD levels in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Treatment increases NAD levels in the brain.

source_record.support_text: The current study by investigating apocynin PKPD in mice demonstrated that apocynin can readily cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB) with logBB values between −0.04 and 1.
One study showed that, following single intra-peritoneal injection (5 mg/kg), apocynin was detected in the brain, but in a glycosylated form.
source_record.extra_details: apocynin was detected in the brain in a glycosylated form

source_record.support_text: Chenodeoxycholic acid and hyodeoxycholic acid are bile acids that can pass through the BBB and can be detected in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: can be detected in the brain

source_record.support_text: Pharmacokinetic studies of clonazepam show that it readily passes the blood-brain barrier, reaching peak brain concentrations within 1-2 h after oral dose.
source_record.extra_details: reaches peak brain concentrations within 1-2 h after oral dose

source_record.support_text: The measurement of drug levels in the CSF showed that NGD 97-1 has relatively low penetration into the CNS, possibly as a result of P-gp mediated efflux.

source_record.support_text: Following peripheral intravenous administration in cynomolgus monkeys, clonidine demonstrated a centrally mediated, dose-dependent reduction in blood pressure, which showed that the agent crossed the blood-brain barrier.

source_record.support_text: Clonidine is considered to transport across the BBB by passive diffusion and has a reported log BB of 0.11.

source_record.support_text: Some substances permeate the blood-brain barrier fairly readily. These include... probably glucose. Glucose is the only substance which will pass into the brain relatively easily in order to support oxidative metabolism adequately in vivo. Myers and Netsky gave a good review and discussion of the dynamic relation of blood and cerebrospinal-fluid glucose (cerebrospinal fluid/blood = .63-.88 glucose ratio).

There is a very effective barrier for glucose that must be overcome by an active transport mechanism. In rats, the glucose concentration in brain tissue (c Gk(H)) was measured at approximately 6·10⁻⁵ g ml⁻¹ (≈ 6 mg-%) compared to a blood plasma concentration of 6·10⁻⁴ g ml⁻¹ (≈ 60 mg-%).
source_record.extra_details: The barrier is overcome by an active transport mechanism; the corresponding blood plasma concentration was 6·10⁻⁴ g ml⁻¹ ≈ 60 mg-%.
