source_record.support_text: GSK588045 dose dependently blocked the signal of the PET ligand [¹¹C]WAY100635, confirming its brain entry and occupancy of 5-HT₁A receptors in the primate brain.
source_record.extra_details: Confirmed brain entry through occupancy of 5-HT₁A receptors.

source_record.support_text: PET studies in monkeys reported that [¹¹C]-2-OH-NPA had very low brain uptake, which was potentially due to its hydrophilic character (cLogD = 0.77).
source_record.extra_details: Compound: 2-OH-NPA; hydrophilic character noted with cLogD = 0.77.

source_record.support_text: MEAI displayed rapid brain influx and a high brain to plasma concentration ratio of 5.5 in male SD rats, reaching a peak brain level of 11 mg/kg within 4-5 min following i.v.-bolus administration.
source_record.extra_details: Following i.v.-bolus administration, MEAI reached a peak brain level of 11 mg/kg within 4-5 min; the brain is described as a fast equilibrating tissue compartment attaining instantaneous steady-state equilibrium.

source_record.support_text: In rats administered 3-(phenylamino)alanine (PAA), very high levels of the compound were observed in the brain (2139 ng/g), indicating the passage of PAA through the blood–brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Dose administered was 5 mg/kg via gastric gavage; analysis performed at 5 h.

source_record.support_text: After administration of 3-(phenylamino)alanine (PAA) by gastric gavage to Wistar rats, the highest concentration of PAA was 12.3 µg/g in the brain, indicating the passage of PAA through the blood-brain barrier.
Compound 53, a bicyclic analogue of 44, exhibited the best CNS penetration observed within this series (brain:blood ratio = 2.6) in mouse.
source_record.extra_details: Compound 53

source_record.support_text: In rats, brain/plasma ratios of D-histidine increased continuously after injection, indicating that D-histidine partitioned into the brain and was very slowly removed from the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Brain/plasma ratios increased continuously; molecule was very slowly removed from the brain.

source_record.support_text: L-histidine is an essential amino acid that readily crosses the blood-brain barrier; following systemic administration of 1000 mg/kg to rats, brain levels of L-histidine were found to be increased by 230%.
source_record.extra_details: Dose administered was 1000 mg/kg.

source_record.support_text: Histidine freely passes across the blood–brain barrier and its brain concentrations can be significantly increased by increasing its plasma concentrations to enable improved NMR measurement.
It has also been shown that histidine easily crosses the blood-brain barrier with a brain uptake index of 33.
In vivo mouse data showed increased brain levels of histidine, which crosses the blood–brain barrier via antiportal transportation with large neutral amino acids through LAT1.
source_record.extra_details: Histidine crosses the BBB via antiportal transportation with large neutral amino acids through the LAT1 transporter.

source_record.support_text: Very low levels of imidol were found in brain and testes of rats, indicating that it was difficult for imidol to cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Very low levels of imidol were found in the brain and testes.

source_record.support_text: Following intravenous injection of [2H6]pyrrolidinone into mice, unchanged pyrrolidinone was found in brain tissue at a concentration of 1.67 µmol per g, supporting the assumption that pyrrolidinone crosses into the CNS.
source_record.extra_details: The quantitative value was specifically reported in Table 1 as 1.67 ± 0.18 µmol/g whole brain after a dose of 200 mg kg-1.

source_record.support_text: After single intravenous administration of aniracetam to rats, 2-pyrrolidinone (PD) was rapidly distributed into the cerebral cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus, exhibiting an AUCbrain/AUCplasma ratio of 53-55%.
source_record.extra_details: The high brain levels of PD suggest it penetrates into the brain.

source_record.support_text: The study of Dilept pharmacokinetics in rats demonstrated that the drug penetrates the blood brain barrier and can be detected in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: The drug was detected in blood plasma for 30 min upon peroral administration.

source_record.support_text: In experiments on rats, the antipsychotic preparation dilept (N-caproyl-L-prolyl-L-tyrosine methyl ester) crossed the blood-brain barrier and was detected in the brain, with a brain/plasma distribution coefficient of 2.0. Transport from the blood to the brain occurred via both free diffusion and the participation of active carriers.
source_record.extra_details: Transport occurs not only by free diffusion, but also with the participation of active carriers.

source_record.support_text: In an in vivo experiment where thiacloprid was administered by intraperitoneal injection to mice at 10 mg/kg, it was confirmed that thiacloprid can pass through the blood–brain barrier, with brain levels of 11 ppm at 15 min, declining to 3 ppm at 60 min, and 0.8 ppm at 240 min.
source_record.quant_value: 11 ppm at 15 min, declining to 3 ppm at 60 min, and 0.8 ppm at 240 min
source_record.extra_details: Administered by intraperitoneal injection at 10 mg/kg.

source_record.support_text: After injection of [¹⁸F]6 in cynomolgus monkeys, radioactivity readily entered brain in a high amount, with approximately 540% SUV present in the caudate at 13 min after injection.
source_record.extra_details: Value was present in the caudate at 13 min after injection.

source_record.support_text: [¹⁸F]FE-PE2I was administered to monkeys and could be visualized in the striatum and midbrain/substantia nigra. Additionally, total brain uptake of [¹⁸F]FE-PE2I was expressed as percent standardized uptake value (%SUV).
source_record.extra_details: The compound was evaluated as a PET radioligand for the dopamine transporter (DAT).

source_record.support_text: In vivo PET imaging of N-methylquipazine (NMQ) in rats and nonhuman primates indicated that its uptake was observed in brain structures known to contain 5-HT3R.

In vivo experiments in rats showed no significant brain uptake for the diastereomers of technetium(V)-oxo-3-[N-(2-mercaptoethyl), N-(N'-(2-mercaptoethyl)-2-aminoethyl)]-amino-propyl 3β-(4-chlorophenyl)-8-methyl-8-azabicyclo [3.2.1]octane-2β-carboxylate, which suggests a drastic reduction of passage over the blood-brain barrier (BBB).
The original acetamide analogue 10 showed a brain to blood ratio consistent with free passage across the blood–brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Data determined via 1 mg/kg iv and 3 mg/kg oral studies in rat.

source_record.support_text: After intraperitoneal administration, levetiracetam quickly appeared in CSF, suggesting ready penetration of the blood–brain barrier. Additionally, the dose-dependent increase in serum and CSF levetiracetam concentrations suggests that transport across the blood brain barrier is not rate limiting over the concentration range observed.
source_record.extra_details: The drug quickly appeared in the CSF and transport across the BBB was not rate limiting over the observed concentration range.

source_record.support_text: In rhesus monkeys, it was observed through the SV2A PET tracer [11C] UCB-J that LEV enters the brain in 23 min.
In rats, LEV was detected in the cerebrospinal fluid, hippocampus, and frontal cortex after intraperitoneal administration.
source_record.extra_details: detected in the cerebrospinal fluid, hippocampus, and frontal cortex after intraperitoneal administration

source_record.support_text: In primates, the time course of [76Br]BrDEX and [76Br]BrLEV in the brain was studied by PET, and it was found that these two radiotracers penetrated rapidly into the brain.
Levetiracetam is rapidly absorbed and transported across the blood-brain barrier, although in rats there is a significant delay between the serum Tmax (0.25–0.50 h) and the CSF Tmax (1.33–1.92 h).
source_record.extra_details: The text notes a significant delay between the time to peak concentration in serum and the CSF.

source_record.support_text: Autoradiographic studies in the rat demonstrated that idazoxan has the capacity to penetrate through the blood-brain barrier, showing rapid uptake of radioactivity from blood to organs such as the brain after intravenous administration of [2¹⁻¹⁴C]idazoxan.
source_record.extra_details: Rapid uptake of radioactivity from blood to the brain was observed after intravenous administration of [2¹⁻¹⁴C]idazoxan.

source_record.support_text: NX-5948 has the capability for penetrating the central nervous system (CNS), making it active against malignant tumors in the brain and able to degrade BTK in intracranial cells. Following oral administration to mice, the levels of NX-5948 detected in the CSF were the same as those of unbound NX-5948 in plasma.
source_record.extra_details: NX-5948 is active against malignant tumors in the brain and degrades BTK in intracranial cells.

source_record.support_text: Perfusion with physiologic saline containing 100-500 µM 4-Cl-KYN for 20 s demonstrated significant brain uptake of 4-Cl-KYN, with an influx mediated by the cerebrovascular large neutral amino acid transporter (L system) and a best fit Vmax of 16.9 ± 2.3 nmol min⁻¹ g⁻¹ in rats.
source_record.extra_details: Transport mediated by the cerebrovascular large neutral amino acid transporter (L system).

source_record.support_text: Perfusion with physiologic saline containing 100-500 µM 4-Cl-KYN for 20 s demonstrated significant brain uptake of 4-Cl-KYN, with an influx mediated by the cerebrovascular large neutral amino acid transporter (L system) and a best fit Km of 105 ± 14 µM in rats.
source_record.extra_details: Transport mediated by the cerebrovascular large neutral amino acid transporter (L system).

source_record.support_text: The three 123I-iodinated agents, including L-[123I]iodo-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline-3-carboxylic acid (ITIC), cross the blood-brain barrier, followed by efflux from the brain. In healthy experimental rats, the brain radioactivity uptake for ITIC was 0.12±0.03% ID/g at 5 min, 0.10±0.01% ID/g at 15 min, 0.18±0.05% ID/g at 30 min, and 0.07±0.01% ID/g at 60 min post injection.

In normal rat tissues, the iodinated agent IAPA crossed the blood-brain barrier rapidly, although it was followed by an efflux from the brain. The accumulation in the brain remained relatively low at less than 0.4 %ID/g.
source_record.extra_details: The agent crossed the BBB rapidly but was followed by efflux from the brain.

source_record.support_text: Compound 12 (clofoctol) was tested in mouse brains after the last i.v. administration of 10 mg/kg body weight, showing brain tissue concentrations of 152-187 ng/g at 5-90 minutes, indicating that clofoctol is permeable in crossing the BBB.
source_record.assay_model: in vivo measurement in mouse brains
source_record.extra_details: Concentrations were measured at 5-90 minutes after the last i.v. administration of 10 mg/kg body weight.

source_record.support_text: All of the esters (MP3A, MP3P, MP3IB, MP3B, MP4A, MP4P, and MP4IB) showed rapid and high uptakes in the brain, with uptakes in three brain regions (striatum, cortex and cerebellum) being about 10% dose/g at 1 min after injection in mice, indicating that the esters possess sufficient lipophilicity for penetrating the BBB.
source_record.extra_details: Uptake measured at 1 min after i.v. injection in the striatum, cortex, and cerebellum.

source_record.support_text: Whole-body autoradiographs in male Swiss Webster mice revealed accumulation of radioactivity in the brain during the first 24 h following exposure to acrylamide.
In ex vivo biodistribution studies using normal ICR mice, the radiotracer (R)-[¹⁸F]5 penetrated the blood-brain barrier (BBB) with a brain uptake of 7.06 ± 0.63 % ID/g at 2 min postinjection.
source_record.extra_details: Measured 2 min postinjection.

source_record.support_text: In a study of healthy volunteers using positron emission tomography (PET), ITI-007 was shown to rapidly penetrate into the brain, with extended, dose-related, and plasma concentration-related striatal D₂ receptor occupancy.
source_record.extra_details: The permeability was evidenced by striatal D₂ receptor occupancy.

source_record.support_text: PET imaging experiments in rats indicated that the isothiazole derivative [¹¹C]LY-2428703 (13) showed rapid uptake and washout in the brain, with a peak cerebellum/forebrain uptake ratio of ~2.
The small-molecule Casein Kinase 1α (CK1α) agonist SSTC3 is described as brain barrier permeable and was observed to accumulate in the brain in medulloblastoma mouse models.
PET imaging in a rat model revealed that the candidate radioligand 4FBox crossed the blood-brain barrier (BBB), although it failed to detect Aβ or α-syn fibrils in vivo.

PAH does not exhibit significant permeation from the circulating blood into the brain across the BBB since the BBB influx clearance of PAH determined by the brain uptake index was 12.1 µl/min/g brain.

Following oral administration in mice, the distribution of piceid in the brain showed that it had the ability to cross the blood-brain barrier, with brain concentrations of 6.07 ± 2.85 µg/g at 10 min, 4.14 ± 2.72 µg/g at 30 min, and 0.33 ± 0.13 µg/g at 120 min.
source_record.extra_details: Route of administration was oral.

source_record.support_text: Diltiazem, a class I compound with good membrane permeability and not an efflux transporter substrate, showed a steady-state unbound brain concentration (Cm,brain) of 0.649 ± 0.127 µmol/L in rats as measured by microdialysis.
source_record.extra_details: Class I compound

source_record.support_text: Diltiazem crosses the blood-brain barrier and is observed in the labyrinth after a labeled intravenous injection in gerbils.
source_record.extra_details: Diltiazem was observed in the labyrinth following the injection.

source_record.support_text: In rabbits, diltiazem was shown to penetrate rapidly into the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) through the blood-brain barrier after i.v. administration, with a CSF/plasma ratio of 0.05–0.2.
source_record.extra_details: Administered via i.v. administration; concentration in CSF reached a peak 5 min after the injection.

source_record.support_text: Diltiazem crosses the blood-brain barrier as demonstrated by autoradiographic studies in the rabbit.
Autoradiographic studies in mice showed that ¹⁴C-labeled diltiazem injected intravenously was distributed to the central nervous system.
source_record.extra_details: The compound was administered as ¹⁴C-labeled diltiazem.

source_record.support_text: In a study using in vivo microdialysis in the frontal cortex of rat brain, 5,6,7,8-tetrahydroisoquinoline (5-TIQ) was detected in brain dialysate about 40 min after intraperitoneal administration, indicating it crosses the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in brain dialysate approximately 40 minutes after intraperitoneal administration.

source_record.support_text: The carotid artery injection study showed that the brain uptake index of YM992 was 141%, indicating a high permeability at the blood–brain barrier (BBB).
In pharmacokinetic studies performed in mouse, AND-302 showed a high brain to plasma ratio, with a value of 2.4 for Cmax.

Oral administration of JNJ-61393215 in rats resulted in time- and dose-dependent occupancy of the OX1R in tenia tecta, indicating sufficient brain penetration, with a brain-to-plasma-concentration ratio ranging from ~0.4 to 0.7.

CL846 entered the brain very rapidly, with maximum concentrations observed at 2.5 min, which was consistent with rapid distribution across the blood-brain interface. The brain tissue:serum concentration ratio for CL846 was 0.52 ± 0.15 and did not vary with time post-administration.
source_record.extra_details: Maximum brain concentrations were observed at 2.5 min post-administration.

source_record.support_text: Peripherally administered diflunisal dose-dependently crossed the blood-brain barrier in mice; however, there was relatively modest penetration, with an average total plasma to brain ratio of ~200:1.
source_record.quant_metric: total diflunisal plasma to brain ratio
source_record.extra_details: Measured via LC-MS/MS after peripheral administration.

source_record.support_text: In mice given a 50 mg/kg dose, free diflunisal brain levels were 196 nM (49 ng/g).
source_record.extra_details: Concentration measured at a 50 mg/kg dose.

source_record.support_text: The radioligand [¹¹C]JNJ7777120 passed the BBB, which shows promise for further PET studies.
In vivo pharmacokinetic experiments in mice showed that compound 5 is able to reach the brain and tends to accumulate in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Administered i.p. 5 mg kg⁻¹; brain/plasma ratio data suggests it tends to accumulate in the brain.

source_record.support_text: Radiolabeled substrates for quantification of P-gp function include ¹¹C-GR218231, which exhibits very low brain uptake under most conditions.
[¹⁸F]FNM (Fluoroethylnormemantine) crosses the blood-brain barrier, and in rats, it demonstrated an uptake in the brain that remains constant after 40 minutes of injection.

Sulphanilic acid normally penetrates the brain in only very small amounts. In mice, concentrations of sulphanilic acid in the brain under control conditions (water) were measured at 0.84, 0.29, and 0.30 mg per 100 g brain.
source_record.extra_details: Baseline control group given water.

source_record.support_text: In rats, biodistribution studies revealed that [¹¹C]3MPICA exhibited low brain uptake, with average regional uptake at 2 minutes reported as 0.19 ± 0.04 %ID/g in the cerebellum, 0.18 ± 0.05 %ID/g in the thalamus, 0.13 ± 0.03 %ID/g in the hippocampus, and 0.11 ± 0.04 %ID/g in the frontal cortex.
source_record.quant_value: Cerebellum (0.19 ± 0.04), Thalamus (0.18 ± 0.05), Hippocampus (0.13 ± 0.03), and frontal cortex (0.11 ± 0.04)
source_record.extra_details: Values measured at 2 minutes post-injection; the authors suggest the carboxylic acid group of the molecule may prevent BBB penetration.

source_record.support_text: In a tissue distribution study following a single intragastric dose of 40 mg/kg, the concentration of demethyleneberberine in the brain of rats was 267.56 ng/g. The results indicated that demethyleneberberine could pass through the blood–brain barrier (BBB) and enter the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Peak concentration measured following a single intragastric dose of 40 mg/kg.

source_record.support_text: In a tissue distribution study following a single intragastric dose of 40 mg/kg, the concentration of demethyleneberberine in the brain of mice was 80.30 ng/g. The results indicated that demethyleneberberine could pass through the blood–brain barrier (BBB) and enter the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Peak concentration measured following a single intragastric dose of 40 mg/kg.

source_record.support_text: Tesevatinib is described as a potent oral brain penetrant; in wild-type (WT) mice, the brain-to-plasma ratio (Kp) was 0.53 two hours after dosing.
source_record.extra_details: Measured two hours after oral or osmotic minipump dosing.

source_record.support_text: In a mouse PK study, compound 40 crossed the blood-brain barrier and exhibited approximately 3 times the exposure compared to that observed in the plasma.

The known TP receptor antagonist S18886 was reported to have poor brain penetration, with a brain/plasma (B/P) ratio of 0.14 when administered at 5 mg/kg to mice and assessed 1 h after dosing via LC-MS/MS.
source_record.assay_model: LC-MS/MS from brain and plasma samples
source_record.extra_details: Dose: 5 mg/kg; measured 1 h after dosing.

source_record.support_text: RO5126946 showed evidence of brain penetration, as assessed by detecting measurable levels of the compound in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of rats.

Trihexyphenidyl is an anticholinergic drug, and positron emission tomographic scanning studies employing labeled anticholinergic drugs have shown that these compounds penetrate the blood brain barrier easily.
source_record.extra_details: Trihexyphenidyl is mentioned as an example of anticholinergic drugs which were shown via PET scanning of labeled compounds to penetrate the blood brain barrier easily.

source_record.support_text: In a study of healthy dogs, Ara-C was able to enter the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and was detected at 24 hours in all dogs.
source_record.extra_details: Ara-C was detected in the CSF at 24 hours in all dogs.

source_record.support_text: Azidothymidine (AZT) has been shown to penetrate the brain, with levels achieved in the CSF being 25% of those found in the serum.
Oral preparations of zidovudine are well absorbed and the drug crosses the blood-brain barrier to reach CSF concentrations that are 50-60% of plasma concentrations.
Compound 6 showed a low mouse brain/plasma ratio (B/P) of 0.16.
source_record.extra_details: Measured 2 hours after 10 mg/kg oral dosing.

source_record.support_text: BMS-204352 crossed the blood-brain barrier in rats with brain-to-plasma (B/P) ratios of approximately 7-11.
Biodistribution studies conducted in awake rats using the carrier-added product [¹⁸F]-1 showed that radioactivity uptake in the brain was high, peaking prior to 15 min.
source_record.extra_details: Uptake peaked prior to 15 min.

source_record.support_text: Following intraperitoneal and intravenous injection of [³H]D,L-pipecolic acid in mice, there is rapid accumulation in the brain, and in absolute terms, 1% of the total radioactivity injected is recovered in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Rapid accumulation was observed following both intraperitoneal and intravenous administration.

source_record.support_text: Following tail vein injection of L-pipecolate in rats, the plasma to brain ratio was 3 at 60 min, indicating that there is a blood-brain transport barrier for L-pipecolate in the rat.
source_record.extra_details: The ratio was measured 60 min after injection; heart contents were 2-3 fold higher than brain contents.

source_record.support_text: Compound 20 demonstrated reasonable brain uptake with a brain to plasma ratio of 0.32 in rat. These results suggested that the intramolecular hydrogen bonds observed in 20 effectively shield the polarity of the molecule, thus improving blood-brain barrier permeability, despite having a high TPSA value (114 Å²).
source_record.extra_details: The brain-to-plasma ratio (Kp) was measured 2 hours after oral administration of 10 mg/kg. The authors note that intramolecular hydrogen bonds shield the molecule's polarity, mitigating the effect of a high TPSA (114 Å²).

source_record.support_text: After administration of α-γ-diaminobutyric acid (DABA) to rats, this compound could be detected in the brain.

After iv injection of [¹¹C]β-CIT-FP in the Cynomolgus monkey, there was a high accumulation of radioactivity in the brain, with 6% of the total radioactivity injected present in the monkey brain six minutes after injection.
source_record.quant_metric: percentage of total radioactivity injected present in the brain
source_record.extra_details: Measurement taken 6 minutes after iv injection.

source_record.support_text: Pioglitazone crosses the blood-brain barrier. A recent study showed that the brain concentration of pioglitazone is affected by P-glycoprotein, a drug efflux transporter; while (+)-pioglitazone is more resistant to this efflux transporter and accumulates in higher concentrations in the brain tissue, (-)-pioglitazone is less resistant and accumulates less.
source_record.extra_details: Transport is mediated by P-glycoprotein. (+)-pioglitazone is more resistant to P-gp efflux and accumulates in higher brain concentrations than (-)-pioglitazone.

source_record.support_text: Pioglitazone exhibits good BBB penetration, with brain concentrations of 712.6 pM ± 231.4 at a 10.2 mg/kg dose and 1007 pM ± 273.4 at a 20.4 mg/kg dose after oral administration.

Due to its high lipophilic property, which leads to increased non-specific plasma protein bindings and vulnerability to P450 metabolism, piperine (PIP) exhibits low blood-brain barrier access, resulting in a low concentration of the compound being observed in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Low brain concentration is attributed to high lipophilicity, increased non-specific plasma protein bindings, and vulnerability to P450 metabolism.

source_record.support_text: pioglitazone has been shown to adequately pass through the blood-brain barrier and maintain adequate concentrations in the brain.
Gromess et al. reported that pioglitazone, a PPARγ agonist, can cross the blood-brain barrier and measured its presence in the brain parenchymal after oral administration in mouse.
source_record.extra_details: Administered via oral route.

source_record.support_text: α-Allocryptopine (peak 5) was detected in CSF, suggesting that it had passed through the blood-brain barrier (BBB) in rats.
In rats, tertiary amine 10a showed high concentration in brain and a good brain-to-plasma concentration ratio (Kp) after 30 min of 0.2 mg/kg intravenous cassette administration.
source_record.extra_details: Dose: 0.2 mg/kg; measured after 30 min. Described as having a good brain-to-plasma concentration ratio.

source_record.support_text: In rats, nifedipine can easily cross the blood-brain barrier, with a peak brain concentration of 37 µg/g wet weight tissue obtained 10 minutes after intravenous injection.
source_record.extra_details: Peak concentration was obtained 10 minutes after administration.

source_record.support_text: The uptake of 4-DAMP by the rat brain is reported as negligible, likely due to the highly polar nature of quaternary ammonium compounds.
source_record.extra_details: The author suggests the negligible brain uptake is due to the highly polar nature of quaternary ammonium compounds.

source_record.support_text: Compound 2r showed a higher degree of brain penetration with a brain/plasma (B/P) ratio of 0.41 in a mouse tissue distribution study.
source_record.extra_details: Sample collected at 2 h.

source_record.support_text: Low activities of 14C in the brain from [14C]ethanolamine administered intravenously show that ethanolamine crosses the blood-brain barrier poorly in the direction of blood to brain.
source_record.extra_details: Poor penetration is attributed to the high polarity of ethanolamine.

source_record.support_text: Pharmacokinetic studies performed in rats demonstrated that Pronetupitant is characterized by a very low blood brain barrier permeability, with a Cmax ratio brain/plasma of 0.045.
Ex vivo autoradiography on mice brain slices and biodistribution studies in rats showed specific uptake of ⁹⁹mTc-TRODAT-1 in striatum and putamen.
source_record.assay_model: Ex vivo autoradiography and biodistribution studies
source_record.extra_details: Specific uptake was observed in the striatum and putamen.

source_record.support_text: Basic PET-CT image analyses indicate that the radioligand [11C]GSK1838705A penetrated the BBB and showed moderate binding in the brain of anesthetized C57BL/6 mice.
source_record.extra_details: The radioligand showed moderate binding in the brain.

source_record.support_text: Evaluation of (E)-5-ethyl-5-(1-[¹²⁵I]iodo-1-penten-5-yl)barbituric acid (12) in female Fischer 344 rats indicated rapid and significant brain uptake of radioactivity within 2 to 5 min, providing a brain blood ratio of ~1. Further studies indicated that this iodovinylalkylbarbiturate does cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Rapid and significant brain uptake of radioactivity was observed within 2 to 5 minutes after intravenous administration.

source_record.support_text: The brain uptake of [¹¹C]beflokatone showed that the tracer freely crosses the blood-brain barrier and binds rapidly to its target sites with a maximum at 30 min.
source_record.extra_details: The tracer binds rapidly to target sites with a maximum at 30 min.

source_record.support_text: [¹⁸F]FDDNP-PET has been found to be able to cross the Blood-Brain-Barrier (BBB) due to its high lipophilicity, permitting it to determine the localization and load of neurofibrillary tangles and senile amyloid plaques in vivo in the human brain.
source_record.extra_details: The compound is able to cross the BBB due to its high lipophilicity.

source_record.support_text: 2-(1-{6-[(2-[18F] Fluoroethyl) (methyl)amino]-2-naphthyl}ethylidene) malononitrile ([18F]FDDNP)-PET can determine the localization and load of neurofibrillary tangles and senile amyloid plaques in the human brain because of its ability to cross the Blood-Brain-Barrier (BBB).
[18F]FDDNP crosses the blood-brain barrier in proportion to blood flow, which was observed during PET visualization in living subjects.
source_record.extra_details: penetration is in proportion to blood flow

source_record.support_text: When administered to humans, PET scanning revealed good brain entry for the probe [¹⁸F]FDDNP.
NBQX administered at 30 mg/kg i.p. produced detectable levels of the parent compound in the CSF of gerbils, with maximum levels of approximately 1 µM detected 30 min after the last dose.
source_record.extra_details: Measured 30 min after the last dose of 3x30 mg/kg i.p. administration.

source_record.support_text: DMSO easily penetrates and goes through the brain, and S35 was detected in the CSF following intravenous injection of labelled DMSO in dogs.
source_record.extra_details: S35 (labelled sulfur) was detected in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) following intravenous injection of DMSO.

source_record.support_text: For compound 12, permeability and brain penetration improved noticeably, with a brain concentration of 3180 ng/g, 1h after oral administration of 10 mg/kg in rats.
source_record.extra_details: 1h after 10 mg/kg dose

source_record.support_text: In SPF male SD rats, geniposide was found to enter the brain tissue through the blood-brain barrier and distribute in the CSF, with a detected CSF content of 58.16±4.38 ng/mL.
source_record.extra_details: CSF collected via occipital macroscopic puncture method after intragastric administration of HLJDD.

source_record.support_text: Nine active components of HLJDD, including berberine, berberrubine, palmatine, jatrorrhizine, baicalin, wogonin, oroxylin A, geniposide, and gardenin B were detected in CSF containing HLJDD, which proved that they could pass the blood-brain barrier to exert effects.
source_record.extra_details: Component is part of the HLJDD prescription.

source_record.support_text: The study clarified that five iridoids, including geniposide, could pass through the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and were detected in rat brain microdialysates and tissue homogenates samples.

Biological studies demonstrated that [¹³N]SD-62 penetrated the blood-brain barrier in its intact form, although it exhibited a low brain-to-blood ratio. Biodistribution data in mice showed brain uptake values of 0.17 (0.05) at 5 min, 0.15 (0.06) at 10 min, 0.20 (0.06) at 20 min, and 0.25 (0.15) at 30 min (% dose/g organ).
source_record.extra_details: The compound penetrated the BBB in its intact form, attributed to high stability against enzymatic hydrolysis. Brain distribution was probably associated with opioid receptors (uptake was prevented by naloxone), and a low brain-to-blood ratio was reported.

source_record.support_text: In PET studies with [11C]nor-β-CIT in Cynomolgus monkeys, there was rapid uptake of radioactivity in the brain, reaching 6% of the injected dose at 15 min, with high accumulation in the striatum, thalamus and neocortex.
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 15 min post-injection.

source_record.support_text: In NHPs, pexidartinib showed limited and variable CSF penetrance, with CSF concentrations ranging from 5.36–16.1 ng/mL, which represented 0.04–0.51% of the observed plasma concentrations at the same time point.

source_record.support_text: In healthy elderly volunteers, functional magnetic resonance imaging results and cerebrospinal fluid levels of S47445 showed that the drug crossed the blood–brain barrier.

source_record.support_text: PET data showed that AG-0029 can rapidly cross the blood–brain barrier and interact with D₂/D₃ and H₃ receptors in the brain of healthy rats.

Although lipophilic, the high protein binding and large molecular mass of anidulafungin preclude extensive penetration into the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), with animal studies reporting undetectable CSF concentrations even at doses significantly higher than those used clinically.
source_record.extra_details: Penetration was undetectable even when using doses significantly greater than used clinically.

source_record.support_text: High CNS penetration was measured for analogue 13, which exhibited a Cub/Cup value of 0.93. This value was determined from AUC-based exposures in WT mice.

source_record.assay_model: concentration measurements in plasma, CSF and hypothalamus

source_record.support_text: In rats, the I-125 labeled compound 15 exhibited a brain/blood ratio of 5.99 at 1 hour after injection, indicating free passage of the compound from blood to cells.

source_record.support_text: AST-004 brain/plasma concentration ratios in other species range from 10 to 30%, indicating distribution of AST-004 into brain tissue.

source_record.support_text: The 5-bromo-6-alkoxy-5,6-dihydro-AZT prodrug (5R,6R)-BMAZT enters the brain more readily than AZT. source_record.support_text: In vivo bio-activities evaluation of the PET probe [11C]1 in rodents using PET imaging demonstrated that the compound has moderate uptake in the brain.

source_record.extra_details: showed moderate distribution in brain and plasma

source_record.support_text: The authors verified that R243 is capable of reaching the brain, noting a remarkably high brain-to-plasma ratio of 35 in wildtype mice. source_record.support_text: In a female CD-1 mouse model, a significant and fast uptake of [18F]3 was observed in the brain within 5 min p.i., measuring 2.20 ± 0.12% of the injected dose per gram of wet weight.
source_record.quant_metric: percentage of injected dose per gram of wet weight
source_record.quant_units: % injected dose per gram of wet weight

source_record.extra_details: The ratio increased over the course of the experiment.

source_record.support_text: The 5-HT6 receptor antagonist SB-742457 showed a good brain/blood ratio (0.5) in rat.

source_record.extra_details: Administered systemically.

Low amifostine concentration was observed in the brain and spinal cord because of the negligible passage of the drug through the blood-brain barrier.

In rats, (–)-stepholidine was extensively transported across the blood–brain barrier, exhibiting good brain penetration and an AUC ratio of brain : plasma of ~0.7, with delivery to the brain measured by microdialysis.
Initial [¹¹C]AZ10419369 PET studies in nonhuman primates demonstrated a high brain uptake.
The first human PET study with [¹¹C]AZ10419369 suggested similarly good in vivo characteristics, and this radioligand displayed rapid uptake.

source_record.support_text: Preliminary PET-measurements in two human subjects confirmed high uptake of [¹¹C]AZ10419369 in brain.

source_record.support_text: [¹¹C]AZ10419369 entered into the primate brain to a high extent, and showed a regional brain distribution consistent with the localization pattern previously reported in autoradiographic studies.

source_record.extra_details: Peak concentrations of meptazinol were attained in the CSF and plasma at about the same time.

source_record.support_text: It was recently shown that βBA is able to pass the blood brain barrier, achieving higher concentrations than AKBA and KBA.

source_record.extra_details: The brain concentration was observed to be sustained.

source_record.support_text: An i.v. dose of gamma-hexachlorocyclohexane administered to the mouse was found to be evenly distributed in the brain, and whole-body autoradiography demonstrated its ability to penetrate the blood-brain barrier.

source_record.support_text: Methylsulphonylpentachlorobenzene was demonstrated to penetrate the blood-brain barrier in mice using whole-body autoradiography, with high concentrations observed in different areas of the CNS.

source_record.extra_details: Ligand of amino acid transporters.

source_record.extra_details: Specific accumulation observed in the striatum.

source_record.support_text: Fluorodopa is an analog of levodopa that crosses the BBB and is stored in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic terminals, and is used in PET scanning to assess graft survival in vivo.
source_record.extra_details: Fluorodopa is an analog of levodopa.

source_record.support_text: FDOPA is reversibly transferred across the blood-brain-barrier by the common carrier of large neutral amino acids (LNAAtransp), with its reversible plasma-to-brain transport defined by the unidirectional blood-brain clearance K1D (mL/g min) and the rate constant for clearance back to circulation k2D (min−1).
source_record.extra_details: Transported via the common carrier of large neutral amino acids (LNAAtransp). Transport is described by K1D (influx) and k2D (efflux).

source_record.extra_details: Uptake was found to be transporter-mediated.

source_record.support_text: The fluoropropyl derivative [¹⁸F]3 revealed a good brain uptake.

In quantitative whole body autoradiography (QWBA), Ticagrelor showed minimal levels in the brain and spinal cord (<0.25 fold of blood levels), and was deemed effectively excluded from the brain and spinal tissues by the blood brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Minimal levels were also observed in the spinal cord and fetus.

source_record.support_text: The A1R antagonist [11C]KF15372 showed a specific and reversible brain uptake, although it had an unacceptably high fraction of nonspecific binding.
source_record.extra_details: The compound showed a high fraction of nonspecific binding that limited its use in preclinical evaluation.

source_record.support_text: In PET studies investigating the cholinergic system in the living human brain, the cerebral uptake of [11C]choline was found to be very low.
Choline exhibits substantial and saturable brain uptake after intravenous injection, with one-pass clearance saturable down to less than 1%.
source_record.extra_details: Substantial uptake reported; uptake is saturable.

source_record.support_text: Choline passes the hematoencephalic barrier very rapidly. Following intravenous injections of labelled choline in rats and mice, brain radioactivity levels rose quickly.
source_record.extra_details: The text notes that choline passes the barrier rapidly despite its electric charge.

source_record.support_text: Exogenous choline enters the brain predominantly in its free form via unidirectional uptake through the blood-brain barrier, utilizing high- and low-affinity carriers. Using AVD, it was determined that approximately 567 nmol/g of choline (0.6% of the administered dose) was taken up into the brain within a short interval of ~30 min.
source_record.extra_details: Uptake represented 0.6% of the administered dose over a short interval of ~30 min; transport is mediated via high- and low-affinity carriers.

source_record.support_text: After i.v. injection of labelled choline in rats, the peak of the specific radioactivity in the brain was reached in less than 1 min, but the specific activity of choline in the brain was only one tenth of that in blood-plasma. These findings led to the conclusion that choline penetrates easily through the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.quant_metric: ratio of specific activity in brain to blood-plasma
source_record.extra_details: The peak of specific radioactivity in the brain was reached in less than 1 min.

source_record.support_text: Following i.v. injection of labelled choline in rats, the maximum radioactivity in the brain was exceeded after 1 min, suggesting that limited permeability of the blood-brain-barrier is not likely to be present.
Radioactive choline injected intravenously into mice enters the central nervous system by a carrier-mediated transport process, suggesting that choline is transported rapidly from plasma to brain.
source_record.extra_details: The text describes a rapid carrier-mediated transport of choline from plasma into the brain.

source_record.support_text: An exchange of choline between brain and plasma has been demonstrated in vivo. After intracarotid administration of [³H]choline in the rat, the passage from blood to brain was found to be saturable and inhibited by choline analogs, indicating a carrier system at the blood-brain barrier level.
source_record.extra_details: Passage from blood to brain was saturable and inhibited by choline analogs.

source_record.support_text: Preclinical investigations by means of [¹¹C]choline in monkeys have shown a low radioactivity brain uptake, about 1% of the injected dose, and a lack of specificity for brain structures.

On the basis of tracing studies done with positron emission tomography (PET), it is known that choline, one of the precursors for the Kennedy pathway, reaches the brain within hours of administration in animals and/or healthy humans.
source_record.extra_details: Reaches the brain within hours of administration.

source_record.support_text: [11C]flumazenil displayed sufficient brain distributions for applications with PET and was successfully used as a PET CNS tracer in humans before it was known to be a P-gp substrate.
source_record.extra_details: Identified as a P-gp substrate.

source_record.support_text: In rhesus monkey, PET images of [11C]UCB-J revealed a high brain uptake throughout the grey matter, with an SUV peak of 5–8 in grey matter areas.
source_record.extra_details: Uptake was observed throughout the grey matter.

source_record.support_text: In human subjects, [11C]-flumazenil shows cerebral uptake with a distribution volume above 0.6 as measured by quantitative positron emission tomography (PET) imaging.
When carrier-free [³H]Ro 15-1788 was administered alone, the tracer passed rapidly into the brain, and blood levels of the tracer were much lower than that observed in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: The tracer was administered as carrier-free [³H]Ro 15-1788; blood levels were observed to be much lower than brain levels.

source_record.support_text: In human volunteers, flumazenil entered the brain readily, reaching peak levels between 5 and 15 minutes after injection. The whole-brain uptake of [¹¹C]flumazenil between 5 and 7.5 minutes after injection was 9.3 ± 3.5% of the injected dose, with an average brain concentration of 6 ± 4 nM.
source_record.extra_details: Average brain concentration of 6 ± 4 nM; peak levels reached between 5 and 15 minutes after injection; rapid ligand uptake observed across a wide variety of gray matter structures.

source_record.support_text: PET imaging studies of [¹¹C]1 (flumazenil) in primates indicated high uptake of activity in the regions of high BZR density such as the cerebellum and cortical regions.
source_record.extra_details: High uptake was observed in regions of high BZR density such as the cerebellum and cortical regions.

source_record.support_text: The radioligand [123I]2 (iomazenil) showed good blood brain barrier permeability, as evidenced by high uptake in brain regions expressing the BZR in rodents, primates and humans.

The selective BZ receptor antagonist Ro-15 1788 is suitable for PET studies because it passes rapidly across the blood-brain barrier, reaching its maximum cortical concentration within ten minutes after bolus injection.
source_record.extra_details: Reaches maximum cortical concentration within ten minutes after bolus injection.

source_record.support_text: [11C]Flumazenil is a radiolabeled benzodiazepine site PET ligand that crosses the blood-brain barrier easily in man in vivo.
source_record.extra_details: The molecule was used as a radiolabeled [11C] PET ligand.

source_record.support_text: Studies using positron emission tomography (PET) in healthy volunteers show that flumazenil has a rapid distribution into, and clearance from, the brain.
source_record.extra_details: The molecule exhibited rapid distribution into and clearance from the brain.

source_record.support_text: [¹¹C]RO 15-1788 rapidly entered the brain after its injection, with very rapid uptake in the occipital cortex as measured by PET.
After i.v. injection of both [¹¹C]flumazenil and [¹⁸F]flumazenil, the brain uptake of radioactivity was rapid, with a peak SUV of whole brain of 4.9±0.9 (mean±s.d.) at 5.5 min for [¹¹C]flumazenil.
source_record.extra_details: Peak whole brain SUV measured at 5.5 min.

source_record.support_text: After i.v. injection of both [¹¹C]flumazenil and [¹⁸F]flumazenil, the brain uptake of radioactivity was rapid, with a peak SUV of whole brain of 4.6±0.9 for [¹⁸F]flumazenil at 5.5 min.
source_record.extra_details: Peak whole brain SUV measured at 5.5 min.

source_record.support_text: In rats, NanoPET/CT imaging showed that [18F]flumazenil radioactivity was detected in all brain regions, and ex vivo biodistribution assays revealed rapid accumulation in the brain at 5 min post-injection. The percentage of ID/g in the brain was 1.92 ± 0.32, 0.39 ± 0.15, 0.03 ± 0.01, 0.03 ± 0.01, 0.001 ± 0.00, and 0.0004 ± 0.00 at 5, 10, 30, 60, 120, and 240 min, respectively.
source_record.assay_model: Ex Vivo Biodistribution Assay and NanoPET/CT
source_record.extra_details: The quantitative values represent brain radioactivity levels at 5, 10, 30, 60, 120, and 240 min post-injection, respectively.

source_record.support_text: In the context of CBZR-PET studies, it is concluded that the only labelled compound able to cross the blood brain barrier is the labelled parent drug, [¹¹C]-flumazenil.
source_record.extra_details: The text explicitly states it is the only labelled compound able to cross the BBB.

source_record.support_text: The intravenous dose of PD156707 attenuates exogenous ET-1-induced vasoconstriction of nonischaemic arterioles, demonstrating that bioactive amounts of PD156707 gain access to the adventitial surface of cerebral resistance arterioles. Furthermore, unpublished observations indicated that ~12% of the plasma-drug level is detectable in the CSF.
source_record.extra_details: The qualitative permeability is inferred from the drug's ability to gain access to the adventitial surface of cerebral resistance arterioles. The quantitative CSF value is based on unpublished observations by T. R. Patel.

source_record.support_text: [18F]2-(6-fluoro-2-oxoindolin-3-ylidene)-N-(4-methoxyphenyl)hydrazine-carbothioamide ([18F]6) showed high brain uptake in ex vivo biodistribution studies in rats.

In CD1 mice, the brain exposure of dictyostatin was found to be AUC₀.₅–₁₆h = 6245 nM-h, which the authors note indicates a possible role for its macrocyclic structure in determining overall brain penetration.
source_record.extra_details: Dosed via 5 mg/kg i.p. administration in CD1 mice. High brain exposure was also explicitly noted in paragraph 7. After 2 hours, brain levels of dictyostatin became comparable to and eventually exceeded plasma levels.

source_record.support_text: In rats, [18F]11 showed rapid brain uptake and limited washout.
source_record.extra_details: Limited washout observed.

source_record.support_text: PET studies in rats showed that polar ¹⁸F-labelled metabolites of [¹⁸F]FDDNP, such as [¹⁸F]fluoroethanol, can penetrate the blood–brain barrier and result in uniform brain uptake.
source_record.extra_details: This compound is a polar radiolabelled fluor ethyl fragment formed from N-dealkylation of [¹⁸F]FDDNP.

source_record.support_text: Radioactive metabolites of [18F]FECNT, including [18F]fluoroethanol, are described as brain-penetrant, which can generate significant radioactive background signals during PET imaging.
source_record.extra_details: Reported as a brain-penetrant metabolite of [18F]FECNT.

source_record.support_text: In vivo methods used to quantify the regional pharmacokinetics in the rat brain showed that AcPAS possessed the ability to enter the brain parenchyma, with a much higher brain concentration and longer t1/2 than PAS.
source_record.extra_details: AcPAS was reported to have a much higher brain concentration and longer t1/2 than PAS.

source_record.support_text: In tissue distribution studies after i.v. administration in mice, Isoliquiritigenin (ISL) showed the lowest levels in the brain, implying that it had difficulty crossing the blood-brain barrier because of its high polarity.
source_record.extra_details: The difficulty crossing the BBB was attributed to high polarity.

source_record.support_text: Biodistribution studies in male Wistar rats demonstrated that CARV hardly entered the brain, with cerebral uptake of radioactivity amounting to 0.08 ± 0.02 (SUV) at 60 min after injection.
source_record.extra_details: Cerebral uptake measured 60 min after injection.

source_record.support_text: [¹¹C]Carvedilol was initially developed as a PET tracer for cerebral beta-adrenoceptor imaging, which was abandoned due to low brain uptake of the molecule.

source_record.quant_value: maximally 3-fold increase after pretreatment with CsA
source_record.extra_details: The compound was also shown to be homogeneously distributed in rat brain via autoradiography.

source_record.support_text: Radiolabeled substrates for quantification of P-gp function include ¹¹C-carvedilol, which exhibits very low brain uptake under most conditions.

source_record.extra_details: Peak brain uptake was observed at 60 min post-injection.

source_record.support_text: Carvedilol can be uptaken in the brain, and autoradiography studies of rat brains showed that it was homogeneously distributed throughout the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Reported as being homogeneously distributed throughout the brain.

source_record.support_text: In zebrafish, AMMOENG 130 was found to penetrate the blood–brain barrier, as significant accumulation in the brain was observed using desorption electrospray ionization–mass spectrometry imaging (DESI-MSI).
source_record.extra_details: significant accumulation in the brain was observed

source_record.support_text: In rats, [¹¹C]RTI-97 showed low brain penetration, as evidenced by an uptake index of 0.5–0.6 for half brain under both baseline and blocking conditions determined by counting after dissection.
source_record.extra_details: These results were noted to be in accordance with low brain penetration determined by PET imaging.

source_record.support_text: Upon intravenous infusion to steady state in rats, FRM-2 brain penetration was severely impaired by P-gp-mediated efflux, with the unbound brain concentration (C_u,b) accounting for only 8% of the unbound plasma concentration (C_u,p).
source_record.extra_details: P-gp-mediated efflux

source_record.support_text: In rat, compound 3 was found to have a significantly higher brain uptake (SUV = 130%), suggesting suitable penetration of the blood-brain barrier (BBB).

source_record.extra_details: Administration dose was 10 mg/m².

source_record.support_text: In healthy male Wistar rats, dipyrone metabolites including 4-acetylaminoantipyrine were measured at high levels in the plasma, CSF and hypothalamus, suggesting that these metabolites cross both the blood-brain barrier and the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier.
source_record.assay_model: concentration measurements in plasma, CSF and hypothalamus

source_record.support_text: Following intravenous administration of bis(t-butyl-SATE)-AZTMP in mice, both the prodrug bis(t-butyl-SATE)-AZTMP and AZTMP were detected in the brain 3 minutes after dosing.
source_record.extra_details: The molecule was detected in the brain 3 minutes after i.v. administration of the prodrug bis(t-butyl-SATE)-AZTMP.

source_record.support_text: In zebrafish brains, acetylcholine showed a relative brain level of 0.02 ± 0.01 ng/mg tissue per 1 mg/L compound exposure.

source_record.support_text: Uptake of orcinol (5 mg/kg) in the brain was qualitatively detected using the HPLC-MS method in mice.

source_record.support_text: After intravenous injection of [¹⁴C]adenosine, only an extremely small fraction of the label was detected in the brain of rats.

source_record.support_text: R-VK4-40 showed excellent brain penetration, achieving a maximum concentration in the brain 2 hours after oral administration at a dose of 10 mg/kg.

source_record.support_text: Compound 25, part of a series of 5,6-dihydro-[1,2,4]triazolo[4,3-a]-pyrazine P2X7 antagonists optimized for good blood-brain barrier permeability, achieved 80% receptor occupancy for 6 h in the brain of rats when dosed orally at 10 mg/kg, as measured by ex vivo radioligand binding autoradiography.

source_record.support_text: Compounds 25 and 26 both showed good brain penetration, achieving brain/plasma ratios of 0.5 in rats.

source_record.support_text: In male Wistar rats, the pharmacokinetic profile of SynuClean-D showed a very low CSF exposure (96.7 h·ng/mL) compared with plasma (372.8 h·µg/mL), with a calculated Ratio CSF/plasma of 0.0003 (0.03%), suggesting that SynuClean-D may have low BBB penetration.

source_record.support_text: Zingerone and its conjugates are distributed throughout body tissues and have shown elevated levels in the brain, indicating the ability of zingerone to diffuse through the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Elevated levels of zingerone and its conjugates were reported in the brain.

source_record.support_text: For BMS-378806, brain penetration was low, with a brain-to-plasma AUC ratio of 0.06 in a brain uptake study using a 5 mg/kg i.v. dose in rats.
