source_record.support_text: PET imaging with [11C] topotecan tracer showed that it only crosses the BBB in healthy mice at a very low level, suggesting that topotecan can minimally cross the BBB.

Pharmacokinetic data in rats demonstrated that the topotecan peak concentration in the brain extracellular fluid was ten times lower than in the blood after intravenous (i.v.) injection, suggesting less than optimal BBB penetration.
source_record.quant_metric: brain extracellular fluid / blood peak concentration ratio
source_record.extra_details: Administered via intravenous (i.v.) injection.

source_record.support_text: Studies in a nonhuman primate model demonstrated that topotecan has excellent CSF penetration, with the active lactone form showing approximately 30% penetration.
source_record.extra_details: The reported penetration percentage refers to the active lactone form of topotecan.

source_record.support_text: In vivo, Mrp4 restricts topotecan movement from the blood into the CSF and from the capillaries into the brain tissue. Mrp4-deficient mice showed enhanced accumulation of topotecan in brain tissue and cerebrospinal fluid.
source_record.extra_details: Topotecan was identified as an Mrp4 substrate; Mrp4 restricts its movement from the blood into the CSF and from the capillaries into the brain tissue.

source_record.support_text: Topotecan has a relatively high penetration into the CSF (30%-40%), and systemic administration has produced antitumor activity in patients with CNS malignancies.
Topotecan was found to penetrate the mouse's blood-brain barrier, reaching a maximal brain concentration of 121.29 ng/g at 0.5 h following an i.p. injection of 10 mg/kg.
source_record.extra_details: Maximal concentration achieved at 0.5 h after i.p. injection of 10 mg/kg.

source_record.support_text: PET with [11C]topotecan showed that its brain uptake was significantly limited by P-gp and Bcrp, as it is a substrate for these transporters.
source_record.extra_details: Topotecan is a substrate for Pgp and Bcrp.

source_record.support_text: Topotecan has been shown to penetrate the blood-brain barrier following systemic administration and to achieve relatively high CSF levels (30% of serum) without associated neurotoxicity.
source_record.extra_details: Following systemic administration; reported without associated neurotoxicity.

source_record.support_text: In a study of plasma and CSF pharmacokinetics of topotecan in non-human primates, it was found that topotecan penetrates the CSF, reaching concentrations that are 32% of those measured in plasma and achieving reasonable penetration of the blood–brain barrier.
A report showed that Mrp4 restricts the penetration of topotecan into the brain and cerebrospinal fluid.
source_record.extra_details: Mrp4 restricts penetration into both the brain and cerebrospinal fluid.

source_record.support_text: Very low levels of VP16-213 were found in the CSF of 12 patients at all time points, and no VP16-213 was detected by HPLC in the CSF of two patients given the drug intravenously.
Topotecan crosses the BBB to elicit documented efficacy in patients with relapsed systemic non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and penetrates the CNS, reaching concentrations in CSF of more than 30% in plasma.
source_record.extra_details: Documented efficacy in patients with relapsed systemic non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.

source_record.support_text: Data from animal models show that topotecan freely penetrates the blood-brain barrier, with concentrations in the cerebrospinal fluid found to be more than 30% of the plasma level after iv infusion.
source_record.quant_metric: CSF concentration relative to plasma level
source_record.extra_details: Measured after iv infusion.

source_record.support_text: Following systemic intravenous administration of 10 mg/m² over 10 minutes in a nonhuman primate model, topotecan penetrated the CSF, and lactone concentration reached 30%.
source_record.extra_details: Lactone concentration reached 30% in the CSF.

source_record.support_text: Topotecan has been shown to cross the blood brain barrier; specifically, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) penetration of the active lactone form of topotecan was approximately 30% after intravenous (IV) bolus in a nonhuman primate model.
source_record.extra_details: The reported penetration value refers to the active lactone form of topotecan.

source_record.support_text: Topotecan, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, is shown to penetrate the CNS, reaching a concentration in the CSF of approximately 30 % of the plasma level.
source_record.quant_metric: concentration in the CSF relative to plasma level

source_record.support_text: Topotecan penetrates the central nervous system (CNS), and 30% of plasma levels were measured in the cerebrospinal fluid (Liquor).
Blaney and colleagues demonstrated that topotecan significantly penetrates into the CSF of nonhuman primates, with a penetration rate of approximately 30%.
source_record.extra_details: Topotecan demonstrated activity against primary central nervous system tumors.

source_record.support_text: A PET probe, [(11C)TPT, was synthesized due to the penetration of Topotecan (TPT) through the blood-brain barrier. Small-animal PET was used to evaluate the P-glycoprotein (Pgp)- and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP)-mediated brain penetration of [(11C)TPT.
source_record.extra_details: Brain penetration is mediated by P-glycoprotein (Pgp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP).

source_record.support_text: Topotecan crosses the blood brain barrier and can be detected in the CSF at cytotoxic concentrations approximating those achieved in plasma.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in the CSF at cytotoxic concentrations approximating those achieved in plasma.

source_record.support_text: Approximately 30% of topotecan crosses the blood-brain barrier and can be detected in the cerebrospinal fluid.
source_record.extra_details: Topotecan can be detected in the cerebrospinal fluid.

source_record.support_text: Central nervous system (CNS) penetration has been demonstrated for topotecan, and its cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) level is 32% of its simultaneous plasma levels.
Topotecan has been shown to cross the blood-brain barrier, and in a primate study, the mean CSF-to-plasma ratio of topotecan exceeded 30%.
Studies using animal models have shown that β-alanine can cross the blood–brain barrier and increase carnosine levels in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: β-alanine was reported to increase carnosine levels in the brain.

source_record.support_text: In humans, the extraction of norepinephrine and epinephrine across the brain, measured with high internal jugular venous sampling, constitutes only a few percent, indicating that a blood-brain barrier to catecholamine extraction exists across the cerebral circulation.
Preliminary organ distribution studies in mice demonstrated a brain uptake of [¹⁸F]7a at 5 min p.i., which was assumed to be sufficient for PET imaging.
source_record.extra_details: Brain uptake at 5 min p.i. was described as sufficient for PET imaging.

source_record.support_text: In primate brain, both [¹¹C]AMP and [¹¹C]PMP freely penetrated the blood-brain-barrier, which was demonstrated using i.v. bolus injections of radiotracer and PET imaging.
Lupeol, stigmasterol, and α-amyrin-acetate demonstrated the ability to traverse the blood-brain barrier (BBB), as evidenced by log BB values > 0.3.
The radioligand [18F]3 (H3-2406), featuring a 4-cyclopentylpiperazin scaffold, demonstrated good brain uptake with an SUV of 2.4 in rat PET imaging studies.
source_record.extra_details: The 4-cyclopentylpiperazin scaffold was credited for providing favorable physicochemical properties and brain uptake.

source_record.support_text: Radioactivity in the brain was negligible after the intravenous administration of the constituent DMAE*.
Mianserin showed a logBB of 0.99, indicating it is brain-penetrating in rat model measurements of steady-state distribution.
source_record.assay_model: steady-state distribution values of rat model measurements

source_record.support_text: [11C]uPSEM792 showed low brain uptake in monkeys with a peak radioactivity of approximately 0.8 SUV.
Following intravenous injection into rats, [¹⁴C]9m6CP exhibited a high brain uptake of 0.7–0.8% ID/g at 1 min after injection, and was concluded to have high BBB permeability.
source_record.extra_details: Transport of the proprobe across the BBB is described as being by diffusion; uptake was measured at 1 min post-injection.

source_record.support_text: PET scans in rats indicated that [18F]GE387 has the ability to enter the brain.
Levels of DIFEQ in the brain of the mouse were very low, measured at 0.003% of the injected dose after 10 min, and the compound is later characterized as having poor uptake in the mouse.
source_record.extra_details: Measured 10 min after injection; qualitative 'poor uptake' confirmed in paragraph 44.

source_record.support_text: Molecular hydrogen (H2) is able to rapidly and readily diffuse across biological membranes and the blood–brain barrier due to its small molecular size and non-polar nature. In rodents, elevated H2 levels in both blood and brain tissue have been detected within minutes after administration.
source_record.extra_details: Permeability is attributed to the molecule's small size and non-polar nature.

source_record.support_text: [¹⁸F]3F4AP displays excellent characteristics for PET imaging including a fast entry and washout from the brain mediated by a pKa value close to physiological (pKa = 7.65) and a positive logD (logD = 0.41).
source_record.extra_details: The compound shows fast entry and washout from the brain; this behavior is attributed to a pKa of 7.65 and logD of 0.41.

source_record.support_text: Focused high resolution brain imaging in Rhesus macaques showed that [18F]3-F-4-AP exhibited fast entry into the brain, with a peak SUV of 3.2–5.5 at 2–5 min.
source_record.extra_details: Peak SUV was observed at 2–5 min post injection.

source_record.support_text: [¹⁸F]3F4AP is a PET radioligand that binds to Kv1 channels and has been demonstrated to readily penetrate the blood–brain barrier of primates.
In a tissue distribution test using tadpoles, cyproconazole was detected in the brain with a distribution proportion of 3%, indicating that cyproconazole could permeate the blood brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: The overall tissue distribution order was gut (56%) > tail (19%) > stomach (9%) > liver (8%) > heart (5%) > brain (3%).

source_record.support_text: In mice, cysteamine was observed to cross the BBB, with a brain transport coefficient (Clup) of 0.15 ± 0.02 µL/g/s as measured by ISCP.
source_record.extra_details: Brain transport measured by directly infusing the brain via the carotid artery.

source_record.support_text: Cysteamine was detected in the brains of rats following gavage feeding of cysteamine.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in the brain following gavage administration of the compound.

source_record.support_text: Following intraperitoneal or intravenous administration of 14C moexipril in rats and dogs, radioactivity was not detected in brain tissue, as moexiprilat does not cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.assay_model: radioactivity detection after intraperitoneal or intravenous administration

source_record.support_text: It was demonstrated with salmonids that considerable concentrations of naphthalene and smaller concentrations of metabolites were present in the brain of juvenile and mature fish.
source_record.extra_details: considerable concentrations of naphthalene and smaller concentrations of metabolites were present in the brain

source_record.support_text: In a study of healthy dogs, the compound CO was able to enter the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). However, it was not detected in the CSF until 144 hours in one dog and until 180 hours in two dogs.
source_record.extra_details: CO was not detected in the CSF until 144 hours in one dog and until 180 hours in two dogs.

source_record.support_text: In a study involving rats given a bolus subcutaneous dose of 40 mg/kg, p-Methoxymethamphetamine (PMMA) exhibited efficient penetration through the blood-brain barrier, reaching a maximum brain/plasma ratio of 15.8 after 8 hours of observation.
source_record.extra_details: Maximum ratio reached after 8 h; dose was 40 mg/kg bolus subcutaneous.

source_record.support_text: Animal studies using 14C-gabapentin demonstrate that plasma and brain tissue concentrations of gabapentin are very similar.
source_record.extra_details: Plasma and brain tissue concentrations were reported to be very similar.

source_record.support_text: Gabapentin possesses some lipophilicity and readily crosses the blood-brain barrier, yielding a CSF: plasma concentration ratio of 0.09 to 0.14 as measured in 5 patients.
source_record.extra_details: The passage notes that gabapentin has some lipophilicity.

source_record.support_text: Gabapentin can readily cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). In vivo studies demonstrated that at a single intravenous bolus dose, the peak concentration of gabapentin in rat brain tissue was 15- to 20-fold higher than that in brain interstitial space sampled by microdialysis.
source_record.quant_metric: peak concentration in brain tissue / brain interstitial space
source_record.extra_details: The transport is predominately mediated by an L-type Na⁺-independent amino acid transporter (system L).

source_record.support_text: Gabapentin readily crosses the blood-brain barrier and is actively transported into the brain tissue via system L, with brain tissue concentrations shown to be similar to or higher than those in the blood.
source_record.extra_details: Actively transported into brain tissue via system L; concentration in brain tissue is similar to or higher than that in blood.

source_record.support_text: Gabapentin crosses the blood-brain barrier by a transporter-mediated mechanism that appears to be saturated at a dose of 100 mg/kg. In rats, forebrain gabapentin content (0.7 mM) achieves 70% of the concentration found in the blood (0.9 mM) measured 2 hours after intraperitoneal injection of 1000 mg/kg.
source_record.extra_details: The transporter-mediated mechanism appears to be saturated at a dose of 100 mg/kg. Brain concentration was 0.7 mM and blood concentration was 0.9 mM.

source_record.support_text: Pharmacokinetic experiments have shown that gabapentin crosses the blood-brain barrier very rapidly and reaches maximal brain levels within 30-60 min, suggesting it is transported by an active transport process.
source_record.extra_details: The rapid penetration into the brain has led to the suggestion that gabapentin is transported by an active transport process.

source_record.support_text: Autoradiographic studies using SK&F 29661 (4) have shown that it is unable to penetrate the blood-brain barrier (BBB), presumably due to its high polarity.
source_record.extra_details: The lack of penetration is presumably due to the compound's high polarity.

source_record.support_text: SK&F 29661 (4) was used as a negative control in blood-brain barrier transport studies, as autoradiographic studies have shown that it is unable to penetrate the BBB in vivo.
Autoradiographic studies have shown that 4 does not penetrate the BBB, presumably due to the high polarity of the 7-aminosulfonyl substituent (π = −1.84).
source_record.extra_details: Lack of penetration is attributed to the high polarity of the 7-aminosulfonyl substituent (π = −1.84).

source_record.support_text: Autoradiographic studies showed that SK&F 29661 (1) did not cross the blood–brain barrier (bbb), presumably due to its low lipophilicity.
source_record.extra_details: Presumably due to its low lipophilicity.

source_record.support_text: The in vivo brain uptake of inosine is measurable, and it is a substrate for a nucleoside carrier present in the BBB.
source_record.extra_details: Transported via a nucleoside carrier.

source_record.support_text: Inosine, a purine nucleoside that readily crosses the blood–brain barrier (BBB), was administered at 250 mg/kg (SC) to rats, resulting in a 1-fold and 1.5-fold increase of inosine within 10 min of administration in the substantia nigra (SN) and striatum, respectively.
source_record.extra_details: Brain exposure was measured in the substantia nigra (SN) and striatum 10 and 20 min after a 250 mg/kg subcutaneous injection.

source_record.support_text: Kim et al. (2013) demonstrated that intravenous administration of inosine induced axon sprouting in the CNS and increased serotonergic input to the lumbar spinal cord, indicating that inosine can cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: BBB permeability was inferred from the observation that intravenous (systemic) administration induced axon sprouting in the CNS and increased serotonergic input to the lumbar spinal cord.

source_record.support_text: Oral administration of inosine to mice transiently increased its concentration in the brain.

In wild frogs (Rana limnocharis), the blood-brain barrier was found to work efficiently to suppress the entry of Dechlorane Plus (DP) into brain tissues, with a liver/brain concentration ratio > 1 (p < 0.05).
Nitroglycerine is a lipid-soluble molecule and hence easily crosses the blood-brain barrier and can be detected in the central nervous system.
source_record.extra_details: Described as a lipid-soluble molecule that can be detected in the central nervous system.

source_record.support_text: In preclinical studies in nonhuman primates, cytarabine CSF concentrations were unmeasurable.

Following i.v. bolus administration of 600 mg/m² ara-C in dogs, the drug demonstrated a distribution phase into the CSF, with a mean CSF: plasma concentration ratio at the time of the CSF peak of 0.58 ± 0.17.
source_record.extra_details: Ratio was measured at the time of the CSF peak.

source_record.support_text: The reported penetration of ara-C across the blood-brain barrier was assessed by measuring CSF concentrations; at two to three hours after infusion of HiDAC, the CSF concentration of ara-C was one to three times that in the plasma.
source_record.extra_details: Measured 2-3 hours after HiDAC infusion.

source_record.support_text: Earlier pharmacologic studies by Ho and Frei indicated that systemically administered ara-C crossed the blood-brain barrier and that the CSF concentration was approximately 40% of the plasma concentration.

Cytarabine was shown to cross the blood-brain barrier in a patient with an Ommaya reservoir, where it was observed that the CSF concentration was 40% of the plasma concentration and rapid equilibration occurred between the two.
source_record.extra_details: Rapid equilibration was noted between plasma and CSF Cytarabine.

source_record.support_text: Systemic administration of chemotherapeutic agents shows very limited penetration of the CNS. Intravenous administration of cytosine arabinoside has a CSF:plasma ratio of only 15% in humans.
Pharmacokinetic data for Cytarabine (Ara-C) indicate slow penetration into the liquor and CSF, with reported CSF/plasma ratios of about 0.15 after 2- or 3-h infusions in doses between 1-3 g/m².
source_record.extra_details: Data based on 2- or 3-h infusions of doses between 1-3 g/m².

source_record.support_text: Early pharmacologic studies by Ho and Frei showed that ara-C equilibrated rapidly between plasma and CSF during standard drug infusion and that the CSF:plasma ratio was 0:4 at steady state.
source_record.extra_details: Measured at steady state.

source_record.support_text: Ara-C readily crosses the blood-brain barrier; specifically, by continuous intravenous infusion, the CSF level of Ara-C at equilibrium was 60% of that in the plasma.
source_record.quant_metric: CSF level at equilibrium / plasma level

source_record.support_text: In humans, Ho et al. showed that CSF concentrations of cytarabine reach 40-60% of those achieved in plasma during continuous intravenous cytarabine infusion. This represents documented penetration of parenterally administered cytarabine into the CNS.
Cytarabine penetration through the blood-brain barrier has been demonstrated, with CSF concentrations reported as 6%-22% of the plasma concentration.
Various agents, including cytarabine, have been shown to enter the brain parenchyma and CSF, and this penetration can be improved by administering high doses of systemic chemotherapy.
source_record.extra_details: Penetration into the brain parenchyma and CSF can be improved by administering high doses of systemic chemotherapy.

source_record.support_text: Ho and Frei demonstrated that cytosine arabinoside crossed the blood brain barrier and that CSF drug levels were 40% of those obtained in plasma; at an infusion rate of 400 mg/m² day the CSF concentration was 0.2 µg/ml.
source_record.extra_details: At an infusion rate of 400 mg/m² day, the CSF concentration was 0.2 µg/ml.

source_record.support_text: Ara-C is described as having a high penetration property into the CNS and the ability to pass the blood/brain barrier, which may contribute to the observed lack of CNS or other extramedullary relapse in the study.
Parent 5 has been shown to have low brain penetration in a rat tissue distribution study, with a brain to blood ratio of 0.065:1.

Both ⁹⁹mTc-PHH and ⁹⁹mTc-MPHH radiocomplexes were able to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). For ⁹⁹mTc-PHH, the highest brain accumulation in healthy mice was 0.47 ± 0.03 %ID/g at 15 min after injection.
source_record.extra_details: Measurement taken 15 min after injection.

source_record.support_text: Following i.v. doses of 14C-ropinirole hydrochloride in the rat, high brain to blood concentration ratios (1.2–1.6) of total drug-related material were observed, indicating that ropinirole was readily able to cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Measured as total drug-related material following intravenous administration.

source_record.support_text: In monkey, plasma and brain concentrations of radioactivity were very similar following an i.v. dose at 1 mg/kg, indicating that ropinirole was readily able to cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Plasma and brain concentrations of radioactivity were reported as very similar following a 1 mg/kg i.v. dose.

source_record.support_text: Previous brain distribution studies in rats and a 10-day oral toxicology study in monkeys showed high ropinirole penetration into the brain, with a blood concentration ratio ranging from 1 to 3, indicating that ropinirole can readily cross the blood-brain barrier without P-gp transporter involvement.
source_record.assay_model: brain distribution studies and oral toxicology study
source_record.extra_details: No P-gp transporter involvement.

source_record.support_text: In vivo brain distribution studies in FVB wild type mice indicated that vandetanib penetration into the brain is restricted by both Bcrp1 and P-gp mediated active efflux at the blood brain barrier (BBB).
source_record.extra_details: Penetration is restricted by both Bcrp1 and P-gp mediated active efflux.

source_record.support_text: Methomyl crossed the blood-brain barrier (BBB) within 30 minutes of challenge, although it showed an approximate 40% difference in blood and cerebral cortex levels 30 minutes postchallenge following administration of 1× and 2× MLD.
source_record.quant_metric: difference in blood and cerebral cortex levels
source_record.assay_model: blood and cerebral cortex levels comparison
source_record.extra_details: Measured 30 minutes postchallenge following administration of 1× and 2× MLD; noted to cross to a lesser extent than aldicarb.

source_record.support_text: Nimodipine penetrates the blood-brain barrier freely; a study in mice indicated that following intravenous injection, brain concentrations of nimodipine were 6-9 times higher than amlodipine.

Nimodipine was detected in low concentrations in the CSF, and the study proves that nimodipine passes into the CSF when given as an intravenous infusion, with a CSF to plasma-concentration ratio of 0.0051 ± 0.0035.
source_record.extra_details: Detected using a sensitive GC-procedure; high protein binding (98%) was mentioned as a factor for the low ratio.

source_record.support_text: Nimodipine could be detected in the brains of gerbils sacrificed soon after drug injection, reaching a peak level within 15 minutes; one hour after a 1-mg/kg dose, the brain drug level was approximately 100 nmol/kg wet wt.
source_record.extra_details: Measured one hour after a 1-mg/kg dose; drug reached peak level within 15 minutes.

source_record.support_text: In humans, nimodipine has been detected in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) following both oral and IV administration, with CSF concentrations being approximately 0.5% of the corresponding plasma concentrations.
source_record.extra_details: The CSF concentration correlates reasonably well with the nonbound drug fraction.

source_record.support_text: Nimodipine crosses the blood-brain barrier, with brain tissue concentrations in the cerebellum measured by mass spectrometry ranging from 3.3–22.3 ng/gm in treated mice.
source_record.extra_details: Concentrations were measured in the cerebellum.

source_record.support_text: Due to its lipophilicity, Nimodipine is capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier and entering brain tissue to a high extent; its concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid is approximately 0.5% of the measured plasma concentration, which corresponds to the free concentration in the plasma.
source_record.extra_details: The concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid corresponds to the free concentration in the plasma.

source_record.support_text: PET studies in Cynomolgus monkeys showed that three radiotracers, including [¹¹C]butylthio-TZTP, crossed the blood-brain barrier freely.
Cotinine is able to pass the blood-brain barrier and has been detected in the brain of rat, cat and mouse after peripheral nicotine administration.
source_record.extra_details: Cotinine was detected in the brain following peripheral administration of nicotine.

source_record.support_text: In a tissue distribution study in rats, the low level of paeonol detected in the brain indicated that it could pass the blood-brain barrier, with a maximum concentration reaching 202.86 ± 59.57 ng/g, although levels decreased rapidly after 10 min and were not detected after 1.0 h.
source_record.extra_details: low level detected in brain; concentration rapidly decreased after 10 min and not detected after 1.0 h

source_record.support_text: An investigation of [18F]92 PET/CT in a diverse cohort of individuals revealed that [18F]92 efficiently crosses the blood–brain barrier and enters the brain within 3 min.
source_record.extra_details: The tracer enters the brain within 3 min and exhibits efficient clearance.

source_record.support_text: In mice treated with 200 mg/kg of 3f, peak concentrations in the brain (~20 µM) were approximately 2 fold higher than those in the plasma over the first 24 h, indicating that the inhibitor freely crosses the BBB.
source_record.extra_details: Peak brain concentrations were approximately 2 fold higher than plasma concentrations over the first 24 h.

source_record.support_text: In a tissue distribution study of sodium tanshinone IIA sulfonate (STS) intravenously administered to healthy Sprague-Dawley rats, results showed that STS had difficulty in crossing the blood-brain barrier.
Compound 11 crossed the blood–brain barrier and was detected in brain 2 h postexposure, although its concentration dropped to almost zero after 8 h.
source_record.extra_details: Compound 11 was detected in the brain 2 hours postexposure, but the concentration decreased to nearly zero by 8 hours.

source_record.support_text: Biodistribution and imaging studies in mice showed little brain uptake of ⁹⁹mTc-CN7DG; because it is positively charged, ⁹⁹mTc-CN7DG cannot cross the BBB.
source_record.extra_details: The compound is positively charged, which contributes to its inability to cross the BBB.

source_record.support_text: In biodistribution studies in mice, radiotracer [¹⁸F]16 displayed high brain uptake and a high brain to blood ratio. It was also demonstrated not to be a substrate for P-gp, as the P-gp inhibitor cyclosporine A showed negligible effect on tracer distribution.
source_record.extra_details: Determined as not a P-gp substrate because cyclosporine A had negligible effect on distribution.

source_record.support_text: Intravenous administration of 2-[¹⁸F]-fluorodexetimide resulted in high brain uptake of radioactivity in mice.
The results of the present study show that [¹⁴C]-labeled BMAA is measured in the brain following acute i.v. bolus administrations, although the transfer of BMAA across the blood–brain barrier is low.

The 1998 study by Kisby et al. reported that BMAA was detected in the cerebrospinal fluid of orally dosed monkeys and in the brain tissue of intraperitoneally dosed rats, suggesting that BMAA is able to cross the blood-brain barrier.

Paul Cox reported that BMAA can cross the blood-brain barrier and was detected in the superior frontal gyrus of patients who died of ALS-PDC, whereas it was absent in brain tissues from healthy individuals.
source_record.extra_details: BMAA was found in the superior frontal gyrus of patients who died of ALS-PDC but not in the brain tissues from healthy people.

source_record.support_text: L-BMAA was detected in the brain tissue of Chamorros who died from ALS-PDC and in Alzheimer’s patients from Canada, which is attributed to the neurotoxin's capability to cross the blood–brain barrier through an active transport mechanism.
source_record.extra_details: L-BMAA was detected in the brain tissue of individuals with ALS-PDC and Alzheimer's disease.

source_record.support_text: β-N-methylamino-L-alanine (BMAA), a natural neurotoxin produced by microbes, can cross the blood–brain barrier (BBB) and was detected in the brains of patients with neurodegenerative diseases.
source_record.extra_details: BMAA was detected in the brains of patients with neurodegenerative diseases.

source_record.support_text: MP3OH and MP4OH (aminoalcohol forms) showed much lower brain uptakes after injection than ester forms, indicating that these N-methylpiperidinols are hydrophilic enough not to cross the BBB.
source_record.extra_details: Described as being hydrophilic enough not to cross the BBB.

source_record.support_text: pyrrolidine and tetrahydropyridine derivatives such as ALX-1161 (21)... [showed] reasonable oral bioavailability in rats... and excellent brain exposure (brain/plasma ratio = 23).
source_record.extra_details: Compound: ALX-1161

source_record.support_text: In vivo biodistribution studies in male NMRI mice showed that negligible brain uptake was observed for [¹¹C]-4 at both 2 and 60 min postinjection.
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 2 and 60 min postinjection in male NMRI mice.

source_record.support_text: S-(+)-carvone was detected in the whole brain and hippocampus following multiple-dose administration, with concentrations of 0.217 µg/mg in the hippocampus and 0.045 µg/mg in the remnant of the brain, indicating the ability of the compound to cross the blood–brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Compound was identified in all study tissues, specifically accumulating in the hippocampus.

source_record.support_text: For the triptan class, rizatriptan showed a rat Kp,uu less than 0.1, which was consistent with previous findings of low in situ brain permeability and high P-gp efflux.
source_record.extra_details: Reported to have high P-gp efflux.

source_record.support_text: For LY451395, cerebrospinal fluid concentrations were quantifiable in healthy male subjects, and the plasma:CSF ratio was 82:1. The compound also demonstrated penetration in the central compartment.
Compound 2 showed impaired CNS penetration, with a reported free plasma concentration to CSF ratio of 5:1, which was attributed to its reduced lipophilicity.
source_record.extra_details: The impaired penetration was linked to reduced lipophilicity.

source_record.support_text: PA values for [¹⁴C]thiourea were measured with the brain perfusion technique and the intravenous injection technique in conscious, unperfused rats; this nonelectrolyte crosses the blood-brain barrier by simple passive diffusion.
source_record.extra_details: Also compared with the intravenous injection technique; noted as a nonelectrolyte.

source_record.support_text: In biodistribution experiments, radioiodinated ligand 6 exhibited good initial penetration of 1.59% ID/g at 2 min and fast clearance from the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Measurement taken at 2 min; compound showed fast clearance from the brain.

source_record.support_text: The brain to plasma unbound concentration ratio of 3a in rats measured in the FIRF assay was ~0.1, indicating impaired CNS penetration.
source_record.quant_metric: brain to plasma unbound concentration ratio

source_record.support_text: Following 14 days of continuous oral gavage administration in mice, the brain levels of 42f were almost more than 10-fold lower than those of enzalutamide, leading to the conclusion that 42f has extremely low blood-brain barrier permeability.

source_record.extra_details: Peak concentration measured in the brain.

source_record.support_text: Oral L-DOPA treatment, administered via a living cricket, resulted in elevated L-DOPA concentrations in various regions of the brain in male Anolis carolinensis lizards, including the brainstem dopaminergic nuclei, locus ceruleus, paleostriatum, nucleus accumbens, hypothalamus, and medial amygdala.
source_record.extra_details: L-DOPA was delivered to the lizards via a living cricket.

source_record.support_text: Carlsson showed that the administration of levodopa (L-dopa), a dopamine precursor that can cross the blood/brain barrier, to dopamine-depleted rabbits restored lost motor activities.

In animal studies and rat models, L-theanine (L-THE) is able to cross the blood-brain barrier via a leucine-preferring transport system in a dose-dependent manner, with brain concentrations reported to increase significantly 30 min postadministration.
source_record.extra_details: Transport occurs via a leucine-preferring transport system in a dose-dependent manner; brain concentrations increase significantly 30 min postadministration.

source_record.support_text: Carlsson demonstrated that L-DOPA, a precursor of dopamine that can cross the blood-brain barrier, could relieve some of the motor impairment in rodents in parallel with restoration of dopamine levels in brain.

L-DOPA, the precursor of dopamine, is commonly labeled with [¹⁸F] or [¹¹C] for PET imaging. After the radiotracer has passed the blood–brain barrier, it is taken up in dopaminergic neurons via the amine acid transporter.
source_record.extra_details: The text specifies that radiolabeled versions of L-DOPA pass the BBB and are subsequently taken up by dopaminergic neurons via an amine acid transporter.

source_record.support_text: In animal experiments, intravenous injection of L-Dopa was found to effectively increase dopamine concentrations in the brain, demonstrating that L-Dopa crosses the blood-brain barrier without difficulty.
source_record.extra_details: L-Dopa is decarboxylated to dopamine within the brain.

source_record.support_text: SLC7A5 also mediates the transport of thyroid hormones and hormone precursors across the cell membrane, L-DOPA across the blood-brain barrier, L-leucine across the blood-retinal barrier, amino acid-polyamine-organocation superfamily pharmaceutical drugs, toxic methylmercury, 3-(18)F-l-α-methyl-tyrosine PET probe in cancer imaging, and others.
source_record.extra_details: Transport is mediated by SLC7A5.

source_record.support_text: In vivo experiments using labelled L-DOPA demonstrated a rapid accumulation of radioactivity in the brain, although most radioactivity disappeared within 24 hours.
source_record.extra_details: Evidence is based on the rapid accumulation of radioactivity in the brain following injection of labelled DOPA.

source_record.support_text: After injection of D-14C-DOPA in rats, the transfer of radioactivity into the brain was much slower than that of the L-isomer, and a uniform distribution of a very low concentration was observed from 30 minutes to 6 hours.
source_record.extra_details: While penetration was poor, D-DOPA showed appreciably longer retention of radioactivity in the brain compared to the L-isomer, potentially due to a much slower rate of metabolism.

source_record.support_text: In biodistribution studies in normal ICR mice, (S)-[¹²⁵I]5 penetrated the BBB with a medium initial brain uptake level of 4.37 ± 0.70% ID/g at 2 min post-injection.
source_record.extra_details: measured at 2 min post-injection

source_record.support_text: In biodistribution studies in normal ICR mice, (R)-[¹²⁵I]5 penetrated the BBB with a medium initial brain uptake level of 3.72 ± 0.31% ID/g at 2 min post-injection.
source_record.extra_details: measured at 2 min post-injection

source_record.support_text: The PET tracer [18F]-SP203 showed rapid uptake into the brain of rhesus monkeys, with the radioactivity residing in mGluR5-rich regions.
source_record.extra_details: Radioactivity resided in mGluR5-rich regions.

source_record.support_text: Initial PET studies in healthy human subjects showed that [18F]SP203 had high BBB permeability (% SUV; ~580).
Compound 14a crosses the blood-brain-barrier, with an in vivo brain-to-plasma ratio of 0.16.
FTS was shown to penetrate the brain, although at concentrations in the micromolar range.
source_record.extra_details: The text notes that these are relatively low concentrations.

source_record.support_text: In the in vivo distribution study in mice, both tracers [11C]A-582941 and [11C]A-844606 showed high brain uptake.
source_record.extra_details: [11C]A-844606 showed higher brain uptake than [11C]A-582941.

source_record.support_text: Y-25130 showed very low brain uptake in vivo owing to its high lipophilicity.
source_record.extra_details: Low uptake attributed to high lipophilicity.

source_record.support_text: There is minimal penetration of SU-5416 into the central nervous system (cerebrospinal fluid) after intravenous injection in nonhuman primates.
source_record.extra_details: Penetration was measured in the cerebrospinal fluid.

source_record.support_text: The compound LM229 was shown to cross the blood–brain barrier in vivo, contributing to the establishment of a novel platform for PET translational studies using rodent transgenic tau models.
There was negligible rat brain uptake of radioactivity after injection of β-(4-[18F]fluorobenzoyl)propionic acid.
Biodistribution studies in mice demonstrated brain uptake for the tracer [¹²³I]-2 (N-(2-Iodoethyl)linoleoylamide), with a maximum value of 1.23%ID/g at 3 min pi.
source_record.extra_details: Maximum value recorded at 3 min pi.

source_record.support_text: Results of the biodistribution study in mice show an extremely high uptake (>14% ID/g in all brain regions) at 2 min p.i. of both [¹⁸F] and [¹¹C]BMP.
source_record.extra_details: Uptake recorded at 2 min post-injection (p.i.) across all brain regions.

source_record.support_text: BIT225 was measured in CSF in two patients at ~4-5 h after the day 10 dose. CSF concentrations were 87.8 and 24.4 ng/mL and the respective CSF/plasma ratios were 2.5 and 1.5%, indicating that BIT225 penetrates the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Measured approximately 4-5 hours after the day 10 dose; absolute CSF concentrations were 87.8 and 24.4 ng/mL.

source_record.support_text: Terasaki and Pardridge measured the brain uptake index (BUI) of DDA and found a value of <2%, concluding that DDA was not measurably transported through the BBB and the transfer rate was slow.
Diaziquone (AZQ) is an alkylating agent that readily crosses the blood-brain barrier; when given intravenously, the CSF to plasma ratio exceeds one.
Compound 1 showed good CNS penetration in the mouse with a brain/plasma (B/P) ratio of 0.54, and exhibited no indication of active efflux.
In a biodistribution study using normal mice, [¹⁸F]DMFC displayed an initial brain uptake (brain₂ min) of 4.43% ID/g and was noted to have favorable blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability.
The lipid-ester derivative of cidofovir, hexadecyloxypropyl-cidofovir (CMX001), has been detected in the CSF after administration.
source_record.extra_details: The compound was detected in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) after administration.

source_record.support_text: In vivo studies using six-week-old wild-type mice showed that inhibitor 3h (CCG-203586) caused a 10% to 17% decrease in brain GlcCer levels after 3 days of treatment, confirming the ability of 3h to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB).
source_record.extra_details: BBB permeability was confirmed via a reduction in brain glucosylceramide (GlcCer) levels (10% at 10 mg/kg/day and 17% at 30 mg/kg q 12 h) after 3 days of intraperitoneal administration.

source_record.support_text: Urolithin B was detected in the brain of rats upon intravenous administration, confirming that this compound can cross the blood brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Compound was detected in the brain.

source_record.support_text: Two compounds, GNF6702 and a new analog NITD689, showed favorable in vivo pharmacokinetics and significant brain penetration, which enabled oral dosing in mouse models of human African trypanosomiasis.
The authors state that anticholinesterases which penetrate the blood-brain barrier, such as paraoxon, decreased the concentration of substance P (SP) in the brain of rabbits.
In rat brain PET imaging, [11C]POX showed initial rapid radioactivity uptake in brain (p:76) and a brain AUC0-15 min of 23.0 ± 1.5.
source_record.extra_details: Compound name: [11C]POX

source_record.support_text: Thompson and colleagues demonstrated the brain distribution of paraoxon using a carbon-11 positron emission tomography tracer ([11C] paraoxon), which indicated rapid entry into the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Brain distribution was measured using [11C] paraoxon as a PET tracer.

source_record.support_text: A clinical study conducted on piglets showed low penetration of cefpodoxime into the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which was approximately 5%.

Compound 8 (MK-4232) is a CNS-penetrant CGRP receptor antagonist that exhibited good rhesus monkey brain uptake in vivo, with approximate SUV values at 80 min of 1.7 in the cerebellum and 0.9 in the white matter.
source_record.extra_details: Compound 8 is also identified as MK-4232.

source_record.support_text: In an experiment using goats, researchers obtained several samples of CSF and observed good penetration of 6-thioguanine (6TG) into the CSF.
Studies in animals and humans have shown that cefoxitin enters the CSF in concentrations which should inhibit or kill most strains of E. coli and Klebsiella.
Brain penetrations of the radioiodinated ligand [¹²⁵I]1, evaluated in normal mice, showed good initial brain penetration of 3.55% ID/g at 2 min post-injection.

source_record.support_text: In a biodistribution study in mice, [11C]remodelin (cLogP = 2.44) was found to have a radioactivity concentration of 4.43% ID/g in the brain at 1 min after injection, indicating that it can pass through the blood-brain barrier and enter the brain.
source_record.extra_details: The radioactivity level was measured at 1 min after injection; the compound has a moderate lipophilicity of cLogP = 2.44.

source_record.support_text: In a first-in-human trial, Vafidemstat's CNS penetration was demonstrated by the cerebrospinal fluid-to-plasma unbound ratio.

source_record.extra_details: Data based on unpublished studies.

source_record.support_text: Compound 8 showed an unacceptable Bu/Pu ratio of 0.11.
source_record.extra_details: Bu/Pu is the unbound brain/unbound plasma AUC ratio.

source_record.support_text: Acetate, propionate, and butyrate have been shown to readily cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). In humans, the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) concentrations of propionate range from 0–6 mM.
source_record.extra_details: Determined using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) or liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS).

source_record.support_text: The presence of propionate in the cerebrospinal fluid of human subjects at concentrations of 2.8 ± 3.2 μM indicates that short-chain fatty acids can cross the blood-brain barrier.
In human, 22 nmol/g of propionate and 15 nmol/g of butyrate are measured in brain by using gas chromatography.

Clear evidence of uptake of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) by the brain was demonstrated in Wistar rats; specifically, propionate, as one of the three significant SCFAs, was detected in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) following injection into the common carotid artery.
source_record.assay_model: injection into the common carotid artery and detection in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)

source_record.support_text: A study on the development of mouse brains and behaviour demonstrated that metabolites of exclusively microbial origin can cross the blood–brain barrier (BBB), and imidazole propionate was specifically detected in the forebrain of those animals.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in the forebrain.

source_record.support_text: Intravenous administration of propionate causes dose-dependent propionate accumulation in the brain of mice.
source_record.extra_details: Dose-dependent accumulation in the brain following intravenous administration.

source_record.support_text: The three main SCFAs—acetate, propionate, and butyrate—have been detected in cerebrospinal fluid, consistent with the statement that SCFAs can easily cross the BBB.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in cerebrospinal fluid.

In vivo analysis in rat indicates that compound 10 maintains a favorable brain/plasma ratio of 0.4–0.6.
Concentration analysis of 7915 in non-human primates showed a CuCSF/Cup ratio of 0.83 ± 0.25, indicating good CNS penetration.
Concentration analysis of 7915 in non-human primates showed a Cub/Cup ratio of 0.69 ± 0.21, indicating good CNS penetration.
In NHPs dosed orally with compound 7, terminal B_u/P_u and CSF/P_u AUC ratios of 0.6 and 0.8 were achieved respectively, showing a high degree of brain penetration.
source_record.extra_details: Reported alongside a B_u/P_u ratio of 0.6.

source_record.support_text: GNE-7915 is described as brain-penetrant, with a reported CSF/plasma unbound ratio of 0.6 in rats following a 0.5 mg/kg intravenous dose.
source_record.extra_details: dose of 0.5 mg/kg; i.v.

source_record.support_text: After a single oral administration of 14C-delamanid to rats, radioactivity was broadly distributed in various tissues, including the central nervous system, indicating that 14C-delamanid permeated the brain blood barrier.

source_record.support_text: A recent publication from the authors' group demonstrated that glyphosate could cross the blood brain barrier (BBB) and was detected in the brain tissue of exposed mice.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in brain tissue of exposed mice.

source_record.support_text: Findings corroborate the ability of glyphosate to cross the human blood-brain barrier (BBB), which was further supported by the detection of the compound in the brain and cerebrospinal fluid of individuals exposed to glyphosate-based herbicides (GBH).
source_record.extra_details: The compound was detected in the brain and cerebrospinal fluid of exposed individuals.

source_record.support_text: The authors conclude that glyphosate is capable of infiltrating brain tissue and that it traverses the blood–brain barrier and accumulates in the brain in vivo in mice.
source_record.extra_details: The study specifically centered on the traversal of the blood–brain barrier and accumulation of glyphosate in the brain.

source_record.support_text: Mice exposed to 125, 250, and 500 mg/kg per day glyphosate via oral gavage for 14 days had glyphosate detected in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Administered via oral gavage for 14 days.

source_record.support_text: Oral administration of glyphosate to mice (125, 250 and 500 mg/kg for 14 days) elevates glyphosate levels (10–50 ng/mg) in the brain, indicating that orally administered glyphosate infiltrates the CNS.

source_record.extra_details: Permeability was inferred from dose-dependent alterations of neurotransmitters (serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine) in specific brain regions.

source_record.support_text: In mice, no unchanged clorazepate could be detected in the brain following i.v. administration.
source_record.extra_details: No unchanged drug was detected in the brain.

source_record.support_text: The results of the study showed that no unchanged clorazepate enters the brain, even after i.v. injection of very high doses, and no clorazepate could be detected in the CSF at plasma concentrations of 2 µg/ml.
source_record.extra_details: No clorazepate was detected in the CSF at plasma concentrations of 2 µg/ml; it serves as a pro-drug of desmethyldiazepam.

source_record.support_text: FTY720-C2 demonstrated the ability to penetrate the blood-brain-barrier within 5 min of delivery in mice, and the compounds were noted to rapidly enter the brain.

source_record.support_text: A PET study indicated that [¹¹C]CMTP (1a) was able to cross the blood–brain barrier and enter the rat brain.

source_record.support_text: Bilastine is considered a non-brain-penetrating antihistamine with very limited penetration across the BBB, attributed to its low lipid solubility and P-gp-mediated efflux from the CNS. Positron emission tomography (PET) studies show its brain H1-receptor occupancy is nearly zero.
source_record.extra_details: Penetration is limited by low lipid solubility and P-gp-mediated efflux.

source_record.support_text: Data from a PET study indicate that bilastine has a very low potential to penetrate the BBB and cause sedation and detrimental psychomotor effects.
source_record.extra_details: The low BBB penetration is associated with a low potential to cause sedation and detrimental psychomotor effects.

source_record.support_text: In a positron emission tomography (PET) study in healthy volunteers, the brain histamine-1 receptor occupancy of bilastine (after a 20 mg dose) was significantly lower than that of hydroxyzine (25 mg) in all five regions of the cerebral cortex, demonstrating the low potential for bilastine to penetrate the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Brain histamine-1 receptor occupancy was significantly lower than that of hydroxyzine (25 mg) following a 20 mg dose of bilastine.

source_record.support_text: Bilastine is a substrate of P-glycoprotein and is expected to have limited penetration across the blood-brain barrier. In rats, 2 hours after oral administration of 14C-bilastine (20 mg/kg), no radioactivity was seen in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Bilastine is a P-glycoprotein substrate; no radioactivity was seen in the brain 2 hours after oral administration of 20 mg/kg 14C-bilastine.

source_record.support_text: PET (positron emission tomography) showed that bilastine has a brain H1 receptor occupancy (H1RO) near to 0% and can thus be considered as a “non-brain-penetrating antihistamine”.

Measurements of cerebral histamine H1-receptor occupancy by positron emission tomography showed that bilastine had the lowest occupancy, contributing to the absence of sedative effects. Second generation antihistamines, including bilastine, also have a low ability to cross the blood brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Cerebral H1-receptor occupancy was measured by PET and was among the lowest for second generation antihistamines.

source_record.support_text: Whole body autoradiography in the mouse at 30 min after a 50- mg/kg i.p. dose of guanethidine-14C showed that the brain did not have detectable levels in the 30-min to 3-hr interval, indicating the existence of an efficient blood-brain barrier to guanethidine.
source_record.extra_details: Radioactivity levels in the brain were undetectable in the 30-min to 3-hr interval following a 50-mg/kg i.p. dose.

source_record.support_text: After intravenous administration of 35 mg/kg guanethidine to rats, the drug did not enter the brain in appreciable amounts. Measured concentrations of guanethidine in the brain were <0.50 µg/g at 2, 8, and 20 hours post-administration.

source_record.support_text: After administration of a single high dose of radiolabeled guanethidine, its autoradiographic localization indicates that it is largely excluded from the central nervous system by the blood-brain barrier.
