source_record.support_text: Despite bryostatin 1's high molecular weight, considerable brain access was observed, with peak brain concentrations exceeding 8% of the peak blood plasma concentrations.
source_record.quant_metric: peak brain concentrations / peak blood plasma concentrations

source_record.support_text: Following i.v. injection of [¹¹C]tetrabenazine in mice, radiotracer uptake into the brain was rapid, with 3.2% of the injected dose present in the brain at 2 min.
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 2 min after i.v. injection.

source_record.support_text: Following i.v. injection of [¹¹C]tetrabenazine in mice, egress from the brain was very rapid, with only 0.21% of the injected dose still present in the brain at 60 min.
source_record.quant_metric: % injected dose still present in brain
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 60 min after i.v. injection.

source_record.support_text: In vivo PET results in humans confirm that the uptake and retention of the radioligand [¹¹C]TBZ are evident in the thalamus and cerebellum.
source_record.extra_details: Uptake and retention of the radioligand were specifically noted in the thalamus and cerebellum.

source_record.support_text: Published PET scan studies conducted in rodents, primates, and humans confirm that TBZ and its active metabolite cross the blood-brain barrier and concentrate mainly in the basal ganglia.
source_record.extra_details: Tetrabenazine and its active metabolite concentrate mainly in the basal ganglia.

source_record.support_text: Tetrabenazine or α-HTBZ were radiolabeled with carbon-11 ([¹¹C]-TBZ), and PET-scan studies in rodents, primates and humans found that radiotracer uptake into the brain was rapid, with 3.2% of the injected dose in the brain at 2 min.
source_record.quant_metric: percentage of injected dose in the brain
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 2 min.

source_record.support_text: Following PET-scan studies in rodents, primates and humans, egress from the brain for radiolabeled Tetrabenazine or α-HTBZ was found to be very rapid, with only 0.21% of the injected dose still present in the brain at 60 min.
source_record.quant_metric: percentage of injected dose still present in the brain
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 60 min.

source_record.support_text: After i.v. injection, [¹¹C]Tetrabenazine ([¹¹C]TBZ) was rapidly taken up into the brain of mice. Similarly, [¹¹C]TBZ showed high brain uptake in the living human brain, with relatively slower clearance from regions of highest VMAT2 concentrations such as the striatum.
source_record.extra_details: The compound was rapidly taken up into the brain and showed relatively slower clearance from regions of highest VMAT2 concentrations.

source_record.support_text: Brain pharmacokinetic studies in mice established the outstanding brain penetration of BRD5814, with an AUC brain/plasma ratio of 7.7.
Brain pharmacokinetic studies in rats established the outstanding brain penetration of BRD5814, with an AUC brain/plasma ratio of 11.0.
SB-590885 (14) was shown to have poor CNS penetration in rat studies, with a brain:blood ratio of 0.14:1.
SB-590885 (14) was shown to have poor CNS penetration in rat studies, with a log BB of -0.85.
γ-Camera imaging showed high brain uptake of E-[¹²³I]IQNP in a Cynomolgus monkey.

After intravenous (i.v.) injection of E-[¹²³I]IQNP in a Cynomolgus monkey, the radioactivity accumulated rapidly in the brain, and at 80 min after injection, 2% of the total radioactivity injected was present in the monkey brain.
source_record.quant_metric: percentage of total radioactivity injected present in brain
source_record.extra_details: Measured 80 min after i.v. injection.

source_record.support_text: In this study, 6-MAM was the major metabolite detected in the brain with a Cmax of 1118.92 ng/mL. This is consistent with MSI findings demonstrating the tissue distribution of 6-MAM across the BBB.
source_record.extra_details: Cmax measured in brain.

source_record.support_text: In this study, 6-MAM was the major metabolite detected in the brain with an AUC of 32178.08 ng×min/mL. This is consistent with MSI findings demonstrating the tissue distribution of 6-MAM across the BBB.
source_record.extra_details: AUC measured in brain.

source_record.support_text: The presence of UE2343 in the CSF samples taken from human subjects confirmed that the compound crosses the blood brain barrier. At plasma Cmax on Day 4 (101 h), the mean UE2343 CSF levels were 33% of the free plasma levels (range: 25–40%).
source_record.extra_details: Measured at plasma Cmax on Day 4 (101 h); compound is 70% bound to plasma proteins.

source_record.support_text: The presence of UE2343 in the CSF samples taken from human subjects confirmed that the compound crosses the blood brain barrier. At plasma Cmax on Day 4 (101 h), the mean UE2343 CSF levels were 10% of the total plasma levels (range: 7–12%).
source_record.extra_details: Measured at plasma Cmax on Day 4 (101 h); compound is 70% bound to plasma proteins.

source_record.support_text: CSF penetration of emestedastat was confirmed in 4 participants at a single time point, with a CSF : free plasma ratio of 0.33.
source_record.extra_details: Measurements were taken from 4 participants at a single time point; these concentrations were estimated to adequately exceed the half maximal inhibitory concentration for enzyme inhibition in the brain at doses from 10 mg twice daily and above.

source_record.support_text: Xanamem is described as a novel brain-penetrant 11β-HSD1 inhibitor, and the use of a specific PET tracer confirmed a high level of target engagement by the drug in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Xanamem is an 11β-HSD1 inhibitor.

source_record.support_text: Etoricoxib was detectable in CSF as early as 30 min after administration and in all 12 subjects by 3 h; at 24 h, etoricoxib was detected in all 12 CSF samples with concentrations ranging between 22 and 48 ng/mL.
source_record.extra_details: The reported concentration range is specifically for the 24 h sample.

source_record.support_text: The study concluded that etoricoxib penetrated into the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) readily, and its CNS exposure was several times higher than that of dexketoprofen.
source_record.extra_details: Administered by mouth; CNS exposure was several times higher than that observed for dexketoprofen.

source_record.support_text: Epotris penetrates the blood-brain barrier in rats, as demonstrated by its presence in the CSF following subcutaneous administration, suggesting that it crosses the barrier sequence-independently.
source_record.extra_details: The passage notes that reversed and scrambled versions of Epotris were also detected in CSF, suggesting sequence-independent BBB penetration.

source_record.support_text: Central nervous system penetration has been shown for etoricoxib in a study in hip surgery where oral etoricoxib dosing led to meaningful concentrations in cerebrospinal fluid.
source_record.extra_details: Oral dosing led to meaningful concentrations in cerebrospinal fluid; etoricoxib is also noted to be highly bound to plasma proteins.

source_record.support_text: The brain uptake clearance of S18986 [(S)-2,3-dihydro-[3,4]cyclopentano-1,2,4-benzothiadiazine-1,1-dioxide] in the rat was found to be high, approximately 20 µl s⁻¹ g⁻¹, measured using the in situ brain perfusion technique.

Using the in situ brain perfusion technique, it was shown that S 18986 intensively crosses the blood-brain barrier, with a high brain uptake clearance (Clup) of around 20 µL S-1 g-1. This uptake likely took place via passive diffusion, and S 18986 was not a substrate of P-glycoprotein.
source_record.extra_details: S 18986 was not a substrate of P-glycoprotein.

source_record.support_text: In vivo brain distribution of bilobalide revealed its ability to penetrate into CNS.
Regarding BBB permeability, a significant level of bilobalide was detected in the rat brain following a single intravenous dose of 8 mg/kg, which indicates the brain uptake of bilobalide.
source_record.extra_details: Detection occurred after a single dose of 8 mg/kg administered intravenously.

source_record.support_text: Terpene-lactones were shown to cross the rat blood–brain barrier, and the concentrations in brain tissue were found to be 98 ng/g for bilobalide.
In the present study, bilobalide, given systemically, evidently reached a sufficient concentration in the brain to suppress the convulsive effect of hippocampal NMDA infusions in rats.
source_record.extra_details: evidence based on suppression of convulsive effect of hippocampal NMDA infusions

source_record.support_text: It was recently reported that bilobalide was detected in the brain after intravenous administration and that the concentration of bilobalide was much higher than those of ginkgolides A and B after the oral administration of EGb761®.
source_record.extra_details: The brain concentration of bilobalide was reported to be much higher than those of ginkgolides A and B after oral administration of the extract EGb761®.

source_record.support_text: Oral application of EGb 761 results in significant bilobalide concentrations (98 ng/g brain) in the CNS of rodents, demonstrating that bilobalide penetrates the blood brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Administered via oral application of EGb 761.

source_record.support_text: [11C]NAD-299 demonstrated rapid brain uptake in regions rich in 5-HT1A.
A PET-study confirms that robalzotan (NAD-299) passes the blood-brain barrier and binds to central 5-HT₁A receptors in a saturable and dose-dependent manner in the primate brain in vivo.
source_record.extra_details: The compound binds to central 5-HT₁A receptors in a saturable and dose-dependent manner.

source_record.support_text: After the injection of [¹¹C]NAD-299, there was a rapid accumulation of radioactivity in the monkey brain, with the radioactivity in the brain peaking at 5 minutes at 3.5% of the injected radioactivity.
source_record.extra_details: Maximal radioactivity in the brain was observed at 5 minutes.

source_record.support_text: Nobiletin crosses the BBB and is found in 3- to 4-fold higher concentrations in the brain than in circulation and the peripheral organs.
source_record.quant_metric: brain concentration relative to circulation and peripheral organs
source_record.extra_details: The compound also has a slow turnover rate in the brain.

source_record.support_text: After administering nobiletin to mice via intraperitoneal and oral routes, measurements of blood and brain concentrations using a photodiode array detector revealed that nobiletin rapidly shifted into both tissues and rapidly moves from the blood to the brain.
source_record.assay_model: concentration measurement in blood and brain
source_record.extra_details: Concentrations were measured using a photodiode array detector; administered via intraperitoneal and oral routes.

source_record.support_text: Using positron emission tomography (PET) to examine the pharmacokinetics of 11C-labeled nobiletin administered to mice, it was confirmed that nobiletin easily crosses the blood-brain barrier and rapidly moves to the brain.
source_record.extra_details: The study used 11C-labeled nobiletin.

source_record.support_text: Analyses using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and positron emission tomography (PET) indicate that nobiletin quickly penetrates the brain and reaches a maximal level within 3-5 min of peripheral administration.
source_record.extra_details: Reaches a maximal level within 3-5 min of peripheral administration.

source_record.support_text: Analyses using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and positron emission tomography (PET) suggest nobiletin penetrates the BBB and reaches a maximal level within 3-5 min after peripheral administration.
source_record.extra_details: Reaches a maximal brain level within 3-5 min after peripheral administration.

source_record.support_text: When nobiletin (50 mg/kg) was administered, intact nobiletin was detected in rat brains within 1 h after dosing, suggesting it can rapidly cross the blood–brain barrier; furthermore, the concentration of nobiletin was 2.4-fold higher in the brain than in plasma.
source_record.extra_details: Dose administered was 50 mg/kg. Nobiletin was detected in the brain for up to 24 h, while it was observed in plasma for up to 9 h, indicating slower elimination from the brain.

source_record.support_text: In a rat model, PET imaging showed that [¹¹C]-labeled nobiletin (1) accumulated in the brain 5 minutes after intravenous injection, indicating that nobiletin or its metabolite was distributed in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Accumulation was described as transient.

source_record.support_text: NBT was detected in the brains of mice following its i.p. or p.o. administration.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in the brain following intraperitoneal (i.p.) or oral (p.o.) administration.

source_record.support_text: Brain penetration of the radiofluorinated ligand [¹⁸F]14, evaluated in normal mice, showed good initial brain penetration (2.43% ID/g at 2 min after injection) with a moderate to low washout rate (2.10% ID/g at 3 h).
source_record.extra_details: The compound is used as the radiofluorinated ligand [¹⁸F]14; the value at 3 hours reflects the washout rate from the brain.

source_record.support_text: The radiofluorinated ligand [¹⁸F]14 displayed good initial penetration of the blood-brain barrier with an initial brain uptake of 2.43 % ID/g at 2 min after tracer injection in normal mice.
source_record.extra_details: Measured 2 min after tracer injection.

source_record.support_text: In microPET/CT imaging studies in naïve C57BL6 mice, 18F-JCN037 was described as brain-penetrant, showing rapid accumulation in the brain with a SUVmean value of 0.85 at 1 min post-injection.
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 1 min post-injection; noted for rapid brain uptake followed by rapid decrease in concentration.

source_record.support_text: In microPET/CT imaging studies in a Sprague Dawley (SD) rat, 18F-JCN037 showed rapid accumulation in the brain with a SUVmean value of 1.19 at 1 min post-injection.
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 1 min post-injection; noted for rapid brain accumulation followed by rapid decrease.

source_record.support_text: In adult male rhesus monkeys, the levels of testosterone in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) remained at 2-3% of total serum concentrations throughout the study, and following an intravenous bolus injection of testosterone, the steroid rapidly entered the CSF.
source_record.extra_details: The quantitative value refers to CSF levels relative to total serum concentrations.

source_record.support_text: The fraction of the plasma level of testosterone measured in the CSF is about 2.5%. Steroids, such as testosterone, may be assumed to pass the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.quant_metric: fraction of plasma level in CSF
source_record.extra_details: Correspondence was found between calculated unbound levels and those in the CSF.

source_record.support_text: Equimolar administration of testosterone showed a rapid absorption into the brain, with the ratio of brain/blood concentration found to be 1.6 at 5 min and 1.8 at 15 min postadministration.
Brain uptake of radioactively tagged hormones has been demonstrated for testosterone.
Following the administration of ³H-T in cynomolgus monkeys, ³H-T was present in all 14 brain areas, with radioactivity recovered from the nuclear fractions.
In a pharmacokinetic study in rats, piperine demonstrated a high degree of brain exposure with a Kp,brain of 0.95.
Piperine demonstrated efficient uptake and high exposure in the brain of SD rats after oral administration, with an AUC0→t of 19121.26 h·ng/g in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: The brain exposure was described as efficient uptake and high exposure; corresponding plasma AUC0→t was 20299.05 h·ng/ml.

source_record.support_text: Piperine demonstrated efficient uptake and high exposure in the brain of SD rats after oral administration, with an AUC0→∞ of 19366.17 h·ng/g in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: The brain exposure was described as efficient uptake and high exposure; corresponding plasma AUC0→∞ was 20480.09 h·ng/ml.

source_record.support_text: Following oral administration in rats, piperine was noted to efficiently penetrate the brain, with a total brain to plasma AUC₀→∞ ratio of 0.95.
source_record.extra_details: Total concentration

source_record.support_text: Following oral administration in rats, piperine was noted to efficiently penetrate the brain, with an unbound brain to plasma AUC₀→∞ ratio of 1.10.
source_record.extra_details: Unbound concentrations

source_record.support_text: Piperine demonstrated high brain penetration potency after oral administration in rats, exhibiting a brain distribution volume of 36.32±1.40 ml/g brain.

Following oral administration, piperine (PPR), piperlonguminine (PPL), and Δα,β-dihydropiperlonguminine (DPPL) were detected in rat brain tissues and were reported to be able to cross the blood-brain barrier.
The authors note that they have previously demonstrated brain uptake of PPI-1011 using [13C]PPI-1011.
source_record.extra_details: Brain uptake was previously demonstrated using [13C]PPI-1011 (Wood et al., 2011b).

source_record.support_text: QWBA imaging of animals following single and repeated administration of [14C]PPI-1011 confirmed that the ether backbone and/or target plasmalogens were able to cross the blood-brain barrier. Whole brain concentrations of total radioactivity were 4 to 6-fold greater than the LLOQ of 0.485 μg Eq/g from 8 through 168 HPD.
source_record.quant_metric: Whole brain concentrations of total radioactivity
source_record.quant_value: 4 to 6 -fold greater than the LLOQ of 0.485 μg Eq/g
source_record.extra_details: Data measured from 8 through 168 HPD after a single dose.

source_record.support_text: QWBA imaging showed that while uptake of metabolized PPI-1011 to non-circumventricular CNS tissues was relatively low, the uptake following 15 doses in the brain was on average 16–18 times higher than after the single dose, proving the drug reaches the brain in a dose-dependent manner.
source_record.extra_details: Comparison between 15 doses and a single dose; indicates dose-dependent brain penetration.

source_record.support_text: Marizomib, a newer proteasome inhibitor, can cross the blood-brain barrier and can be detected in the CNS upon systemic therapy.
Marizomib, a reversible proteasome inhibitor, has shown improved penetration of the BBB with a CSF concentration of 30%.

In a quantitative whole-body autoradiography (QWBA) study in Sprague-Dawley rats, the distribution of radioactivity to the CNS was ~30% of that for steady-state blood levels, demonstrating that marizomib is able to cross the BBB.
source_record.quant_metric: Distribution of radioactivity to the CNS
source_record.extra_details: The quantitative value is expressed relative to steady-state blood levels.

source_record.support_text: In animal studies, marizomib distributed into the brain at 30% of blood levels in rats. These preclinical studies demonstrated that marizomib can cross the blood-brain barrier in rodent brain.
Several studies have shown that the novel proteasome inhibitor marizomib can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) after systemic administration.
source_record.extra_details: detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) after systemic administration

source_record.support_text: Systemic administration of marizomib was shown to cross the BBB in preclinical animal models.
source_record.extra_details: Administered systemically.

source_record.support_text: In non-tumour bearing Sprague-Dawley rats injected with ³H-NPI-0052, radioactivity was very low/undetectable in the brain, spinal cord and eye.

Marizomib is currently the only proteasome inhibitor in clinical trials that can permeate the blood-brain barrier. In animal studies, marizomib distributed to the brain at 30% blood levels in rats and significantly inhibited (>30%) baseline chymotrypsin-like proteasome activity in monkey brain tissue.
source_record.extra_details: Also reported to significantly inhibit (>30%) baseline chymotrypsin-like proteasome activity in monkey brain tissue.

source_record.support_text: Following acute intraperitoneal administration in mice, 4'-demethylnobiletin was detected in the brain, demonstrating that the metabolite can cross the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Detection of the molecule in the brain following acute ip administration was used to demonstrate BBB penetration.

source_record.support_text: 4'-demethylnobiletin, a bioactive metabolite of NBT, was detected in the brain of mice following acute intraperitoneal administration, indicating that it can cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB) to reach the brain.
source_record.assay_model: brain detection following acute intraperitoneal administration
source_record.extra_details: Identified as a bioactive metabolite of NBT.

source_record.support_text: 4'-demethylnobiletin, a bioactive metabolite of NBT, was detected in the brains of mice following its i.p. administration.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in the brain following intraperitoneal (i.p.) administration.

source_record.support_text: 4'-demethylnobiletin was detected in the brain within 10 min after mice received an i.p. injection of it, indicating that 4'-demethylnobiletin can reach the brain and thereby exert its activity against neurodegeneration.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in the brain within 10 min after i.p. administration.

source_record.support_text: In vivo PET imaging in WT mice showed rapid accumulation of radioactivity in the brain, demonstrating the capacity of [11C]4 to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB).
source_record.extra_details: The compound exhibited rapid brain accumulation followed by a relatively fast wash-out.

source_record.support_text: Dynamic whole-body PET imaging studies performed in WT mice confirmed the BBB penetration capacity of [11C]4, with %ID/cm3 values peaking at 3.7 ± 0.1% around t = 40 s.
source_record.extra_details: Peak concentration occurred at approximately t = 40 s.

source_record.support_text: Metabolism and biodistribution studies in female wild type (WT) mice using dynamic PET-CT imaging confirmed the ability of the BChE inhibitor [11C]4 to cross the blood brain barrier (BBB) and its rapid washout from the brain.
source_record.extra_details: demonstrated rapid washout from the brain

source_record.support_text: In a biodistribution study using normal mice, [125I]5 showed poor blood brain barrier (BBB) permeability and poor initial brain uptake of 0.32% dose/g at 2 min after injection.
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 2 min after injection.

source_record.support_text: Biodistribution studies using normal mice demonstrated that [¹²⁵I]5 displayed poor initial brain uptake.

The four remaining compounds (6l, 6o, 6r, and 7e) were evaluated for brain exposure in rat, utilizing oral dosing (10 mpk) and sampling at a 2 h time point. With the exception of 7e, all compounds gave very low total brain levels (5% or less).
Bi-pyridyl 6l and pyrazole 6r, also have quite poor CSF levels relative to the free plasma concentrations (<10%).
source_record.quant_metric: CSF levels relative to the free plasma concentrations

source_record.support_text: In pharmacokinetic studies in the dog, the brain uptake of trimetrexate was found to be restricted, with brain levels reaching only 2% to 5% of those in plasma.
Pharmacokinetic studies in rhesus monkeys showed that the CSF penetration of trimetrexate was poor.
DORA 50 showed high brain penetration in preclinical species, with a reported CSF/P ratio of ~ 0.04 in rats.
DORA 50 showed high brain penetration in preclinical species, with a reported B/P ratio of 1.1 in rats.
Nevirapine has demonstrated consistent penetration into the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
source_record.extra_details: Consistent penetration into the CSF was reported.

source_record.support_text: Using MADLI-TOF, it was observed that nevirapine (NVP) was able to penetrate the blood–brain barrier at 0.25 h and showed a wide distribution in the brain.
NNRTIs such as nevirapine are of special interest due to their ability to be detected in the CSF.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in the CSF

source_record.support_text: The NNRTI nevirapine is a small molecule with less protein binding than PIs, and reaches effective CSF concentrations.
Efavirenz and nevirapine penetrate into the CSF in concentrations that probably are sufficient.

In Sprague-Dawley rats, Nevirapine (NVP) demonstrated rapid bio-distribution in the brain with a brain Cmax of 1923 ng mL⁻¹ at a Tmax of 0.25 h. Imaging Mass Spectrometry (MSI) confirmed that NVP penetrated and localized in brain regions associated with HIV-associated neurodegeneration.
source_record.extra_details: Tmax was 0.25 h; plasma Cmax was 6320 ng mL⁻¹.

source_record.support_text: The plasma-to-brain concentration ratios of nevirapine in rats and monkeys were shown to be close to 1, supporting the conclusion that nevirapine readily crosses the BBB.

In a separate study, nevirapine has been shown to cross the blood-brain barrier, achieving concentrations in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that are equivalent to unbound concentrations in plasma (plasma protein binding ~ 60%).
source_record.extra_details: plasma protein binding ~ 60%

source_record.support_text: Nevirapine has been shown to penetrate CSF, with minimum concentrations above at least the IC50 of wild-type virus.
source_record.extra_details: Minimum concentrations in CSF were reported to be above at least the IC50 of wild-type virus.

source_record.support_text: Drugs with demonstrated adequate CSF penetration include zidovudine, abacavir, efavirenz, nevirapine, lopinavir/ritonavir, darunavir/ritonavir, dolutegravir, and maraviroc.
source_record.extra_details: Reported as having adequate CSF penetration.

source_record.support_text: Teniposide showed poor penetration into the cerebrospinal fluid, with levels ranging from 0.03 to 0.55% (< 1%) of the simultaneously determined plasma levels after low or high dose administration.
source_record.extra_details: The poor penetration is attributed to high protein binding and/or poor penetration through biological membranes.

source_record.support_text: Only very low concentrations of teniposide, or none at all, have been detected in CSF.
In rats, the distribution of ramosetron to the brain was much lower than to other organs, and the cerebrum-to-plasma concentration ratio was 0.17 at 5 min after intravenous administration.
source_record.extra_details: Measured 5 min after administration.

source_record.support_text: YM060 showed very low brain uptake in vivo owing to its high lipophilicity.
source_record.extra_details: Low uptake attributed to high lipophilicity.

source_record.support_text: Ramosetron is described as a 5-HT₃ receptor antagonist with limited BBB permeability. In female rats, CSF measurements using HPLC revealed low levels of ramosetron after a 0.1 mg/kg dose, while levels were significantly increased following a 1 mg/kg dose.
source_record.extra_details: The authors used HPLC to measure ramosetron levels in the CSF; detectable levels were achieved at higher doses, while low levels were observed at 0.1 mg/kg.

source_record.support_text: TNG908 demonstrates in vivo brain penetration in rodents, exhibiting a Kpuu of ~0.15. It is characterized by high passive permeability and is not a substrate for P-gp or BCRP efflux transporters.
source_record.extra_details: High passive permeability; not a substrate for P-gp or BCRP efflux transporters.

source_record.support_text: TNG908 demonstrates in vivo brain penetration in non-human primates, exhibiting a Kpuu of ~0.6. It is characterized by high passive permeability and is not a substrate for P-gp or BCRP efflux transporters.
source_record.extra_details: High passive permeability; not a substrate for P-gp or BCRP efflux transporters.

source_record.support_text: Tissue distribution analysis in rats showed that neoeriocitrin could transfer across the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Detected using a UPLC-MS/MS method after oral administration of TFDR.

source_record.support_text: After oral administration of TFDR in rats, neoeriocitrin could be detected in the brain, illustrating that it could transfer across the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in 8-month-old and 18-month-old rats after oral administration of TFDR.

source_record.support_text: In dogs, multiple dose intravenous injection of allopurinol achieved a significant drug concentration in CSF, with a CSF to plasma ratio of 0.70-0.80 at 24 h, which indicates a significant transport across the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.quant_metric: CSF to plasma ratio of allopurinol concentration
source_record.extra_details: Measured at 24 h.

source_record.support_text: In vivo brain uptake of allopurinol was measured using intracarotid bolus injection, showing a BUI of 10.4 ± 1.23 at a concentration of 0.096 mM.
source_record.extra_details: Concentration: 0.096 mM. Transported via the blood-brain barrier adenine transport system.

source_record.support_text: Tetracycline crosses the blood-brain barrier; in patient K. P., the cerebrospinal fluid concentration was 1.02 mg./cc. while the simultaneous blood level was 1.9 mg./cc.
source_record.extra_details: Simultaneous blood level was 1.9 mg./cc. for patient K. P.

source_record.support_text: Tetracycline crosses the blood-brain barrier; in patient E. B., the cerebrospinal fluid concentration was 0.324 mg./cc. while the simultaneous blood level was 0.78 mg./cc.
source_record.extra_details: Simultaneous blood level was 0.78 mg./cc. for patient E. B.

source_record.support_text: Tetracycline crosses the blood-brain barrier; in a second measurement for patient K. P., the cerebrospinal fluid concentration was 0.9 mg./cc. while the simultaneous blood level was 1.9 mg./cc.
source_record.extra_details: Simultaneous blood level was 1.9 mg./cc. for patient K. P.

source_record.support_text: Tetracycline crosses the blood-brain barrier; in one unnamed patient, the cerebrospinal fluid concentration was 0.124 mg./cc. while the simultaneous blood level was 0.528 mg./cc.
source_record.extra_details: Simultaneous blood level was 0.528 mg./cc.

source_record.support_text: Norfloxacin concentrations in the liver, kidney and lung of mice 1-4 h after subcutaneous or oral administration exceeded plasma concentrations, whereas the drug was undetected in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Drug was undetected in the brain.

source_record.support_text: In rats, norfloxacin concentrations in the liver, kidney and lung 1-5 h after a single s.c. or intravenous dose exceeded serum concentrations, whereas the drug was not detected in the brain.
source_record.extra_details: Drug was not detected in the brain.

source_record.support_text: In pigs, norfloxacin concentrations were very low in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF); the tissue-to-plasma concentration ratio in the CSF was 0.08 as determined by microbiological assay 4 hours after a single intramuscular injection of norfloxacin nicotinate.
source_record.extra_details: Measured in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) 4 hours after a single intramuscular injection of norfloxacin nicotinate at 14 mg/kg.

source_record.support_text: Norfloxacin brain ECF concentrations were much lower than the corresponding plasma concentrations in rats, with an average AUC_ECF Brain/AUC_plasma ratio of 8.2 ± 5.8%.
Vincristine showed even more limited penetration into the blood-brain barrier structures than cyclosporin; the penetration of vincristine into the brain was noted as very limited.
source_record.assay_model: intravenous bolus injection technique of Ohno et al. (1978)

source_record.support_text: Low brain uptakes were observed for vincristine in the present study.

source_record.support_text: Initial evaluation in rhesus monkey showed that both [¹¹C]LSN3316612 and [¹⁸F]LSN3316612 radioligands showed high brain uptake with a high proportion of specific binding to OGA.

source_record.support_text: Intravenous administration of [¹¹C]LSN3316612 into a rhesus monkey at baseline resulted in good brain radioactivity uptake, with continuous accumulation of radioactivity in the frontal cortex, striatum, hippocampus, and thalamus.

source_record.support_text: Intravenous administration of a low dose of LSN3316612 in rats and subsequent analysis with an in vivo/ex-vivo LC-MS/MS method showed rapid brain uptake, with uptake in the frontal cortex measured at 4.0 standardized uptake value (SUV) at 5 min and 1.9 SUV at 90 min after injection.
source_record.extra_details: Brain uptake was followed by moderately slow washout; peak tracer uptake in frontal cortex (4.0 SUV) was higher than in cerebellum (1.9 SUV).

source_record.support_text: LSN3316612 is an OGA inhibitor reported to have excellent brain exposure; its radioactive form was tested in PET for imaging of animals and human.
source_record.extra_details: The radioactive form of this compound was tested in PET for imaging of animals and humans.

source_record.support_text: After intravenous injection of [18F]LSN3316612 in eight healthy human subjects, good overall brain radioactivity uptake and distribution were observed.

PET imaging with [¹⁸F]LSN3316612 demonstrates its good brain uptake and it has been evaluated in mice, monkeys, and humans. In rhesus monkeys, whole-body PET imaging illustrated high uptake in the brain, particularly in the amygdala, striatum, and hippocampus.
source_record.extra_details: High uptake observed in the amygdala, striatum, and hippocampus of rhesus monkeys.

source_record.support_text: Evaluation of [¹⁸F]4 ex vivo and in vivo revealed low brain uptake of the compound; no differences in brain uptake and retention were detected between APP23 and WT mice.

source_record.support_text: In preliminary dynamic PET imaging studies in rats, the ligand [18F]4 rapidly penetrated the blood-brain barrier.

source_record.support_text: In C57/BL6 mice, PAC-1 administered via the lateral tail vein resulted in a brain concentration of 47.3 ± 5.4 ng/mg tissue 5 minutes post-injection. These results suggest that BBB penetration is a prerequisite for the observed transient neuroexcitation induced by PAC-1.

source_record.support_text: Veterinary trials involving pet dogs showed that procaspase-activating compound-1 (PAC-1) was able to penetrate the blood-brain barrier.

source_record.support_text: In a study using in vivo microdialysis in the frontal cortex of rat brain, 1-benzyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline (1-BnTIQ) was detected in brain dialysate about 40 min after intraperitoneal administration, indicating it crosses the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Detected in brain dialysate approximately 40 minutes after intraperitoneal administration.

source_record.support_text: Systemic ibudilast affects glial cells in the brain and spinal cord, suggesting it crosses the blood-brain barrier. source_record.support_text: Under baseline conditions, the brain uptake of [11C]-N-desmethyl-loperamide is minimal in humans, monkeys, and mice, except in the pituitary of monkeys and humans and the choroid plexus of humans.
source_record.extra_details: Minimal uptake observed except in the pituitary (monkeys, humans) and choroid plexus (humans).

source_record.support_text: In humans, the concentration of radioactivity in the brain after injection of 11C-dLop was low, with a low rate of brain entry (K1 = 0.009 ± 0.002 mL·cm⁻³·min⁻¹), which is consistent with 11C-dLop being a substrate for P-gp.

source_record.support_text: P-gp almost completely blocks brain entry of the PET radiotracer ¹¹C-N-desmethyl-loperamide (¹¹C-dLop), and brain uptake of radioactivity was negligible at baseline in healthy volunteers.
source_record.extra_details: The molecule is a radiotracer used to quantify P-gp function.

source_record.support_text: The radiotracer [¹¹C]N-desmethyl-loperamide (dLop) is a specific substrate for P-gp, and while its brain uptake is minimal in monkeys and humans, it is markedly higher after the administration of the P-gp inhibitor tariquidar.

source_record.support_text: [11C]desmethylloperamide ([11C]dLop) is an avid substrate for P-gp at the blood-brain barrier, and its brain uptake under normal conditions is so low that reductions in uptake due to increased P-gp function are not measurable.
source_record.extra_details: Described as an avid substrate for P-gp.

source_record.support_text: In a baseline PET experiment with [¹¹C]³ in monkey, the uptake of radioactivity in all examined brain regions was very low. These data are consistent with [¹¹C]³ behaving as a substrate for P-gp at the blood-brain barrier.
source_record.extra_details: Baseline brain uptake was very low, but increased dramatically upon administration of the P-gp inhibitor DCPQ. In contrast, uptake into the pituitary, which partially lies outside the blood-brain barrier, was high and not influenced by P-gp inhibition.

source_record.support_text: [11C]HM demonstrated good brain uptake in rats, as evaluated by autoradiography ex vivo and in preclinical PET.

source_record.support_text: For imaging the central nervous system, radiopharmaceuticals must be able to specifically pass through the BBB; [11C]HM ([11C]Hydromethidine) was developed for ROS imaging in the central nervous system, with PET images in mice showing radioactive signals that reflect ROS levels in the brain.
